1 Stern eye **Tip:** During transport, use a boat cover to prevent any items from blowing out of the boat, or make sure to store any items inside the storage compartments and securely close the compartments.
- Be sure the access port cap is properly installed (see page 126 for more information) and the rear platform hatch is closed securely.
- Be sure any cargo that must be carried in the boat as well as the all hatches are secured.
- While traveling, check the wheel hubs on the trailer whenever you park.
If a hub feels abnormally hot, have the bearing inspected before continuing your trip.
On longer trips, it is a good idea to carry a set of spare wheel bearings, seals, and races.
- When making a turn, do not cut corners.
The trailer has a smaller turning circle, so it turns more sharply around the corner than the towing vehicle.

# 153. Backing your trailer

It takes practice to back a trailer successfully.
If you are not familiar backing up with a trailer, practice first in an open area away from obstacles.
[Manual09_253]
**Keep the following points in mind when backing up:**
- Back slowly.
Make steering adjustments in small steps.
- Turn the towing vehicle’s wheels opposite the direction you want the trailer to go.
- After the trailer begins moving, turn the towing vehicle to follow it.
- Have a second person stand by to help direct you with hand signals.

# 154. Launching

As a courtesy to other boaters, prepare your boat for launching before using the ramp.
Each launch may have particular differences, such as ramp angle, prevailing wind, waves, and water currents.
If possible, watch a couple of boaters launch their boats first to notice any problems.
While every boater develops a preferred launch procedure, here is a recommended general procedure:
[Manual09_254]

(1) Perform the pre-operation checks shown on page 85 that can be performed on land.

(2) Remove all trailering tie-down lines from the boat and attach your docking lines and fenders, if used.

(3) Disconnect the trailer lights from the towing vehicle.

(4) Back the trailer down the ramp as close to 90 to the shoreline as you can.
If possible, have a second person stand aside as an observer.
Stop when the wheels are at least halfway submerged.
Set the parking brake.

(5) Remove the bow line from the bow eye.

(6) Back the trailer farther into the water until just the tops of the fenders show, and then reset the parking brake.
Board the boat and start it.
If possible, remain on the trailer until the engines are warm and are responding to throttle.

(7) Back the boat out into the water, watching carefully for people, other boats, or obstacles.

# 155. Loading

(1) Disconnect the trailer lights from the towing vehicle.

(2) Back the trailer down the ramp as close to 90 to the shoreline as you can.
If possible, have a second person act as an observer while standing to the side of the trailer.
Stop when the tops of the trailer’s fenders are about 3 inches above the waterline.

(3) With the boat moving at the slowest idle speed, guide the boat onto the support rails.
Use throttle only if necessary for steering ability.
**Warning:** Using too much throttle can cause the boat to jump over the front of the trailer, which can result in injury to the boat operator and bystanders.

(4) Make sure the boat is centered on the support rails and is headed straight for the bow stop (bumper board).
Ease the boat forward until the bow rests against the bow stop.
**Notice:** The winch line is not designed to pull the boat onto the trailer.

(5) Attach and tighten the winch line.
**Notice:** The winch line should not be the only line securing the bow during trailering.
Use the chain along with the winch to secure the boat to the trailer.

(6) Pull the trailer up the ramp out of the way of other boaters.
Attach the bow and stern tie-downs.
Reconnect the trailer lights.

# 156. Lifting

**Notice:** Do not attach lifting cables to the bow eye, cleats, stern eyes, ski tow hook, or handgrips.
Serious damage to the boat can occur.
Use only a sling designed specifically for lifting boats.
If you need to remove the boat from the water without a trailer, use these guidelines:
- Use a sling-type lifting mechanism designed for lifting boats.
The sling should be covered with a protective material to prevent damage to the hull gelcoat.
- Use spreader bars to avoid side stress to the hull that may cause cracks in the gelcoat and fiberglass.
- Attach guidelines to the bow eye and stern eyes to control movement of the boat during lifting.
- Remove all people and all cargo from the boat.
Drain any excess water from the bilge using the bilge pump.
- Be sure all people are standing clear, and then lift the boat slowly and just far enough to verify that the boat is securely held and properly balanced.
If necessary, lower the boat again and adjust the slings.
- When ready, lift the boat slowly and carefully.

# 158. Flushing the cooling system

Cooling system flushing is essential to prevent the cooling system from clogging up with salt, sand, or dirt.

(1) Connect the garden hose adapter to a garden hose.

(2) Loosen the flush hose connector cap and remove it.

(4) Make sure that the area around the boat is clear, and then start the engine.
Immediately after the engine starts, fully turn the water supply on so that water flows out continually from the jet thrust nozzle and cooling water pilot outlet.
**Notice:** Never turn on the water before starting the engine.
The water could flow back through the muffler into the crankcase causing severe engine damage.

(7) Stop the engine.

The water could flow back through the muffler into the crankcase causing severe engine damage.

# 161. Battery care

If the boat will not be used for more than a month, remove the battery and store it in a cool, dark place.
The battery is located in the battery compartment.
To remove the battery:

(1) Turn the battery switch to the OFF position. (See page 30.)

(2) Disconnect the ground lead (black) and the negative (-) battery lead (black).

(3) Disconnect the positive (+) battery lead (red).

(4) Unfasten the battery strap, and then remove the battery from the boat.
[Manual09_262]
1 Positive (+) battery lead (red)
2 Battery strap 3 Negative (-) battery lead (black)
4 Ground lead (black) To store the battery:

(1) Clean the battery casing and terminals using a mixture of baking soda and water (one tablespoon of baking soda to one cup of water).

(2) Apply dielectric grease or petroleum jelly to the battery terminals and to all exposed connectors.

(3) If the battery will be stored for a longer period, check its state of charge (use a hydrometer or a voltmeter and load tester) at least once a month and recharge the battery if it gets too low.
To charge the battery:

(1) Remove the caps from the cells.
Add distilled water if necessary to top up the electrolyte to the proper level.

(2) Follow the battery manufacturer’s instructions for charging.
**Warning:** When charging a battery, keep it well away from sparks and open flames, as it gives off explosive gases.
When using a battery charger, connect the battery to the charger before you turn on the charger.
This will prevent sparking at the terminals that could ignite battery gases.
To install the battery:

(1) Place the battery in the battery holder, and then fasten the battery using the battery strap.

(2) Connect the positive (+) battery lead (red) to the positive (+) battery terminal.
**Notice:** Reversal of the battery leads will damage the electrical parts.

(3) Connect the negative (-) battery lead (black) and the ground lead (black) to the negative (-) battery terminal.

(4) Make sure that the battery is securely held in place.

# 162. Long-term storage

Storing your boat for prolonged periods of time, such as winter storage in freezing temperature, requires preventative maintenance to ensure against deterioration.
It is advisable to have the boat serviced by an authorized Yamaha Boat Dealer before storage.
However, the following procedures can be performed by the owner with a minimum of tools.

# 163. Fuel system

Fill the fuel tank with fresh fuel, adding one ounce of Fuel Med RX, available from your Yamaha Boat Dealer, to each gallon of fuel or use an equivalent according to the manufacturer’s instructions. (See page 78 for information on filling the fuel tank.) Do not “top off” the tank, because fuel could spill.
A full fuel tank is less likely to allow condensation to collect in the tank, reducing the chance of contaminated fuel.
Running the engine with treated fuel during cooling system flushing will also help protect the fuel system. **Tip:** Use of Fuel Med RX eliminates the need to drain the fuel system.
Consult a Yamaha Boat Dealer or other qualified mechanic if the fuel system is to be drained instead.

# 164. Lubrication

It is advisable to take the boat to a Yamaha Boat Dealer to have the engine fogged for long-term storage.

# 172. Jet pump clean-out procedure

**Warning:** Severe injury or death may result if you ignore any of the following:
- Turn off and remove both main switch keys, remove the clip from the engine shut-off switch, and wait for all movement to stop before removing the access port caps.
- Never override the interlocks to run the engines with the rear platform hatch open.
- The impellers have sharp edges.
Be careful when reaching into jet pump areas.
If weeds or debris get caught in the intakes or impellers, cavitation can occur, and though the engine speed rises, forward thrust will decrease.
If this condition is allowed to continue, jet pump damage can occur and the engines may overheat and seize.
If there is any sign that a jet intake or impeller is clogged with weeds or debris, follow this clean-out procedure.

(1) Turn off and remove the main switch key, remove the clip from the engine shut-off switch, and wait for all movement to stop.

(2) Open the rear platform hatch. (See page 63.)

(3) Check that the retaining cord is securely attached to the access port cap and strap eye.
[Manual09_275]
1 Retaining cord 2 Strap eye

(4) While holding the handle and pushing down, turn the access port cap counterclockwise until the “SET” mark is aligned with the slot, and then lift the cap by the handle. **Notice:**
- Do not lift or pull the cap with the retaining cord.
- Set the cap where it cannot be accidentally knocked overboard.
[Manual09_276]
1 “SET” mark 2 Slot
[Manual09_277]
1 Access port cap

(5) Remove any weeds or debris from the drive shaft, impeller, pump housing, and jet thrust nozzle.
If you cannot remove the debris, consult a Yamaha Boat Dealer.

(6) To reinstall the access port cap, first clean off any sand or other foreign matter from the cap or port surfaces.
Apply a light coat of Yamalube Waterproof Marine Grease (P/N: ACC-GREAS-10-CT), if available, to the seal of the access port cap.
If grease is not available, apply the grease during the post-operation checks.

(7) Insert the cap so that the “SET” mark is aligned with the slot, and then while pushing the handle turn the cap clockwise until the “SET” mark is aligned with the edge of the access port.
[Manual09_278]
1 “SET” mark 2 Slot 3 Edge of the access port

(8) Check that the cap is perpendicular to the centerline of the boat.
Pull the handle forcefully to make sure that the cap is locked securely.
If a strong pull will move the access port cap, it is not locked securely—the cap could be forced out by water pressure during operation.
[Manual09_279]
1 Perpendicular to the centerline of the boat

(9) Close the rear platform hatch. **Notice:** Be sure the access port caps are locked securely in place.
Otherwise, the caps could be forced out of the access ports by water pressure, causing loss of performance and possible damage. **Tip:** The rear platform hatch has interlocks to shut off the engines should the hatch be accidentally opened during operation.
The engines will not restart unless the hatch is closed and latched.

# 173. Jump-starting

**Warning:** Severe injury or death may result if you ignore any of the following:
- If the blower will not operate, ventilate the engine compartment by opening the engine hood for several minutes before attempting a jump-start.
- Do not connect the negative (-) jumper cable to the negative (-) terminal of the dead battery.
Sparks could ignite battery or fuel vapors, which could cause an explosion.
If the boat battery runs down, the engine can be started in an emergency using a 12-volt booster battery and jumper cables.
To connect the jumper cables:

(1) Connect the positive (+) terminal of the dead battery to the positive (+) terminal of the booster battery with the positive (+) jumper cable.

(2) Connect one end of the negative (-) jumper cable to the negative (-) terminal of the booster battery.

(3) Connect the other end of the negative (-) jumper cable to an engine hanger.
**Notice:** Be sure all connections are secure and correct before attempting to start the engine.
Any wrong connection may damage the electrical system.
[Manual09_280]
1 Negative (-) jumper cable 2 Positive (+) jumper cable 3 Engine hanger 4 Booster battery

(4) Start the engine, and then disconnect the jumper cables by reversing the above steps.
**Notice:** Do not turn the main switch key for more than 5 seconds.
If the engine does not start in 5 seconds, release the main switch key and try again after 15 seconds.
Continuous cranking for more than 5 seconds will discharge the battery and the engine will not start.
The starter motor may also be damaged if it is engaged continuously for more than 5 seconds.

# 174. Fuse replacement

**Warning:** Do not use fuses of a higher amperage than recommended.
Substitution with a fuse that has an improper rating can cause extensive electrical system damage and possible fire.
If a fuse is blown, replace it with the proper fuse.
To replace a fuse:

(1) Open the engine hood. (See page 56.)

(2) Unfasten the band.

(3) Remove the fuse box from the air filter case by pulling the fuse box toward the bow.

(4) While pushing both sides of the fuse box cover inward, pull the cover toward the bow and remove it.

[See page 66.])

(7) Install the fuse box cover.

(8) If the accessory fuse or bilge pump fuse was replaced, install the fuse holder.

(9) Install the fuse box to the air filter case.

(10) Fasten the band.

(11) Close the engine hood. **Warning:**
- The operator of the towing boat must keep speed to a minimum and avoid traffic or obstacles which could be a hazard to either boat.
- The towing line should be long enough so the towed boat will not collide with the towing boat when slowing down.
The boat should be towed only if it becomes inoperative.
The towing rope should be long enough so that the boat will not collide with the towing boat when slowing down.
A good rule of thumb is a tow rope which is three times the combined length of the towing boat and the boat.
Tow the boat using the bow eye only.
Tow the boat at a no-wake speed.
**Notice:** Do not tow the boat at speed fast enough to leave a wake (8 km/h, 5 mph).
Severe engine damage could result because water can flood the non-operating engine through the water intake.

# 1. Introduction, notes, features, and accessories

Thank you for purchasing the Color E-Reader. Read this user manual before using the device so that you understand its basic operation, supported file formats, charging requirements, and care instructions.

All pictures and graphics in this manual are simulated and are not intended to specify included applications or content. Technical information and specifications are subject to change without notice.

Notes:

1. If the device cannot power on for the first time, charge it with the USB cable until the battery indicator is full.
2. Handle the reader with care to prevent screen damage.
3. Do not remove the built-in battery while the device is charging.
4. The built-in battery is replaceable, but replacement must be performed by the manufacturer. Contact the manufacturer by phone or email if battery replacement is needed.
5. Contact the manufacturer if you encounter a problem with the device. Do not disassemble the device yourself.

Special features:

- E-book formats: TXT, EPUB, PDF, FB2, HTML
- Audio formats: MP3, WMA, WAV, AAC, and other supported audio formats
- Photo formats: JPEG
- Video formats: AVI, RMVB, MPEG2
- Voice recording format: AAC

Included accessories:

- Leather carrying bag
- USB cable
- AC power adaptor

# 2. Device description and controls

The front, navigation, and bottom views of the device are shown in [Manual13_0], [Manual13_1], and [Manual13_2].

Front view controls:

1. Home/ESC button: Press this button to cancel a prompt, exit a sub-interface, or return to the previous interface.
2. Previous/Next Page buttons: Press these buttons to open the previous or next page.
3. Navigation/Menu button: The navigation button is a four-way control button for left, right, up, and down. The Menu button is used for menu access and confirmation.
4. Zoom in/out: Zoom in or out of a JPEG file. This button also increases or decreases the font size of e-book content.
5. Rotate: Rotate an e-book between horizontal and vertical views.
6. 3.5 mm earphone jack: Connect earphones for private listening. Earphones are not included.
7. USB port: Use the USB cable to charge the device and connect it to a computer for content transfer.
8. Micro SD card reader: Compatible with Micro SD and SDHC cards up to 16 GB.
9. Play/Pause button: Start or pause music playback or voice recording.
10. Power button: Press and hold for 3–5 seconds to power the device on or off.
11. Volume + button: Press to increase the volume when playing music.
12. Volume - button: Press to decrease the volume when playing music.
13. Reset On/Off switch: Located on the back of the device next to the card reader. Use it to reset the device to factory defaults when minor device problems occur.
14. Speaker: 0.5 W audio output.
15. TFT LCD display screen: 7-inch diagonal display.

section_path: 3. Charging the battery and replacing the battery
text:
# 3. Charging the battery and replacing the battery

The e-book reader battery has been partially charged at the factory. The battery indicator is located on the upper-right side of the main menu when the device is turned on. The indicator shows the remaining battery power.

If the battery indicator shows fewer than two bars, charge the device with the USB cable connected to the AC adaptor or a computer. Unplug the USB cable after the device is fully charged.

To charge the device through a computer:

1. Connect the device to the computer with the USB data cable.
2. Use the “Safely Remove Hardware” icon in the Windows taskbar to safely remove the USB mass storage device.
3. After the device switches to USB charging mode, a charging battery icon appears on the e-book reader screen.

Charging through a computer usually takes longer than charging through the AC adaptor. Do not remove the battery while charging is in progress.

Battery replacement:

This device includes a rechargeable 3.7 V, 2000 mAh lithium-polymer battery. If the battery needs to be replaced, contact the manufacturer. Do not attempt to replace the battery yourself. Battery replacement must be performed by the manufacturer’s technician.

section_title: 4. Powering the device on and off and using basic buttons
section_path: 4. Powering the device on and off and using basic buttons
text:
# 4. Powering the device on and off and using basic buttons

To power the device on or off:

1. Slide the Power On/Off switch to On.
2. Press and hold the Power button for about 5 seconds, then release the button to turn the device on.
3. To turn the device off, press and hold the Power button for about 5 seconds.
4. If you do not plan to use the device for an extended period, slide the Power On/Off switch to Off.

Basic button operation:

1. Navigation: Use the four-way navigation keys to move left, right, up, and down.
2. Confirm/Enter: Press the “M” key to enter the currently selected function or refresh the screen.
3. ESC: Press the Home/ESC button to return to the previous screen.

# 5. Main menu and browser history

The main menu displays the device functions, including Browser History, eBook, Music, Video, Photo, Record, Explorer, and Settings. Select the desired function, then press the “M” button to enter. See [Manual13_3].

Browser History displays recently browsed files. Move the navigation keys to select a book, then press the “M” button to open it. The device will go to the last page read in the selected book. See [Manual13_4].

Note: If a recently read file was stored on a Micro SD card and has been deleted, the record may remain in the Browser History list, but the file cannot be opened.

section_title: 6. Reading eBooks and using reading tools

text:
# 6. Reading eBooks and using reading tools

The eBook function supports EPUB, FB2, HTML, PDF, and TXT files.

To select and read a book:

1. Open the eBook function.
2. Select the desired book.
3. Press the “M” button to start reading.

Page navigation:

- Press the Previous/Next Page buttons to turn pages.
- You can also use the Up and Down buttons on the navigation control to turn pages.

Reading menu:

When in eBook mode, press the “M” button to open the reading menu. Available options include Page Jump, Save Mark, Load Mark, Del Mark, Browser Mode, Flip Time, Brightness, and Set Color. See [eReader_08], [Manual13_5], and [Manual13_6].

Page Jump:

1. Press the “M” key.
2. Select “Page Jump”.
3. Press the “M” button again.
4. Enter the desired page number.
5. Press “M” to go to that page.

Bookmarks:

- Save a bookmark: In eBook mode, press “M”, select “Save Mark”, then press “M” again to add the current page as a bookmark.
- Load a bookmark: In eBook mode, press “M”, select “Load Mark”, then press “M” again to open the saved bookmark list. Select the desired bookmark and press “M”.
- Delete a bookmark: In eBook mode, press “M”, select “Del Mark”, select the bookmark to delete, then press “M” to confirm.
- Bookmark capacity: The device allows up to 8 saved bookmarks. When the limit is reached, a newly saved bookmark overwrites the oldest bookmark.

Other reading tools:

- Zoom: Press the Zoom button to change the font size. Available sizes are Small, Medium, and Large.
- Rotate: Press the Rotate button to rotate the screen horizontally or vertically.
- Browser Mode: Select either Auto Mode or Manual Mode.
- Flip Time: Select 10 seconds, 15 seconds, 20 seconds, 25 seconds, or 30 seconds.
- Brightness: Select one of five brightness levels.
- Set Color: Select one of five text colors for reading comfort.

# 7. Playing music

Open the audio file list from the main menu, select the desired audio file, then press “M” to play it. See [Manual13_7] and [Manual13_8].

You can add audio files by connecting the device to a computer with the USB cable, then dragging and copying the desired audio files onto the device.

Supported audio formats include MP3, WMA, WAV, AAC, and other supported formats. The device can play audio while you read an e-book, browse photos, or use the menu.

Music controls:

- Adjust volume: Press the Up/Down navigation keys or the Up/Previous Page and Down/Next Page buttons to adjust the volume.
- Play/Pause: Press the Play/Pause button to pause or continue playback.
- Forward/Backward: Press and hold the Left navigation key to rewind. Press and hold the Right navigation key to fast-forward.
- Previous/Next file: Press and release the Left navigation key to go to the previous audio file. Press and release the Right navigation key to go to the next audio file.

Music play modes:

In Music mode, press “M” and select the desired mode to adjust it. Available modes include Repeat Mode, Play Mode, MS EQ, EQ Sel, and User EQ Setup.

# 8. Playing videos

Go to Video and press the “M” key to enter Video mode. The device supports AVI, RMVB, and MPEG2 video formats. See [Manual13_9].

Video options:

- Subtitle language: If subtitles are available in the video file, press “M”, then select Subtitle Language to change the subtitle language.
- Select Time Play: Press “M”, then select Time Play to change the playback time.
- Full Screen: Press “M”, then select Full Screen to change the display mode. Available modes are Full Screen, Normal, and Original.
- Brightness: Select one of five brightness levels for comfortable viewing.

# 9. Viewing photos

Go to Photo and press the “M” button to enter Photo mode. The device supports JPEG and BMP image formats. See [Manual13_10].

Photo controls:

- Previous/Next photo: Press the Left or Right navigation key to go to the previous or next photo.
- Rotate photo: Press the Play/Pause key to rotate the photo counterclockwise.
- Zoom in/out: Press the Zoom button to zoom in or out of the photo.

Note: Some large files require more time to rotate than smaller files. Large photo files may also take longer to load in the photo viewer.

# 10. Recording voice and playing recordings

To enter voice recording mode, select Record in the main menu and press the “M” button. See [Manual13_11] and [Manual13_12].

To start and save a recording:

1. Press the Play/Pause button to start recording.
2. Press Play/Pause again to pause recording.
3. Press Home to stop recording.
4. After recording is stopped, the device prompts you to save the recording.
5. Select “YES” or “NO”, then press the “M” key to confirm.

To play a recorded file:

1. Go to the main menu and select Music.
2. Press “M” to enter the Music menu.
3. Select Record and press “M” to enter the recorded file list.
4. Select the desired recorded file and press “M” to start playback.

# 11. Using display settings

Select Settings from the main menu and press the “M” button to enter system settings mode. The settings menu includes Display Settings, System Settings, Language, System Information, Auto-shut Time, Time, and Calendar. See [Manual13_13].

To change display settings:

1. Select Display Settings.
2. Press the “M” button to open the Display Settings menu. See [eReader_01].
3. Select Light Time. Available options are 5 seconds, 10 seconds, 15 seconds, 20 seconds, 30 seconds, and Always On. Select the desired time and press “M” to confirm.
4. Select Brightness. There are 5 brightness levels. Select the desired brightness level and press “M” to confirm.

section_title: 12. Using system settings, language, time, date, and calendar
section_path: 12. Using system settings, language, time, date, and calendar
text:
# 12. Using system settings, language, time, date, and calendar

To change system settings:

1. Select System Settings.
2. Press the “M” button to enter the system settings menu. See [eReader_02].
3. Select Restorable to restore the device to factory default settings. Back up all data before restoring the system.
4. Select Key Lock Time to change key locking time. Available options are 10 seconds, 30 seconds, 5 minutes, 10 minutes, and No Locking. Select the desired option and press “M” to confirm.

Language settings:

The device provides several on-screen languages, including English, Chinese, Deutsch, Portuguese, French, Spanish, and other languages. In the system settings menu, select Language, choose the desired language, and press “M” to confirm. See [eReader_03].

System information:

System Information displays the device version information, product brand, company name, software version, memory size, and other device information. See [eReader_04].

Automatic shutdown time:

Available automatic shutdown times are 3 minutes, 5 minutes, 10 minutes, 15 minutes, and 20 minutes. Select the desired time and press “M” to confirm. See [eReader_05].

Time settings:

The Time Settings screen displays the current system time. Use the Up, Down, Left, and Right navigation keys to change the hour and minute, then select “YES” to confirm.

Date settings:

The Date Settings screen displays the current system date. Use the Up, Down, Left, and Right navigation keys to change the year, month, and day, then select “YES” to confirm. See [eReader_06].

Calendar:

Select Calendar, then press the “M” button to enter the calendar. See [eReader_07].

section_title: 13. Connecting the e-book reader to a computer and managing files
section_path: 13. Connecting the e-book reader to a computer and managing files
text:
# 13. Connecting the e-book reader to a computer and managing files

To connect the e-book reader to a computer:

1. Connect the device to the computer with the USB data cable.
2. The reader turns on automatically and displays “USB Connection”.
3. After the connection is complete, the computer identifies the reader as a removable disk.
4. If a Micro SD card is inserted, the computer shows two removable disks: one for the built-in internal memory and one for the Micro SD card.

To manage files:

1. After the device is properly connected to the computer, open My Computer.
2. Select the removable disk for the device or Micro SD card.
3. Transfer, copy, or delete files between the device and the computer as needed.

section_title: 14. Inserting and using a Micro SD card
section_path: 14. Inserting and using a Micro SD card
text:
# 14. Inserting and using a Micro SD card

You can expand the memory of the device up to 16 GB by inserting a Micro SD or SDHC card. A Micro SD card is also called a TF card.

To insert a Micro SD card:

1. Power off the device.
2. Insert the Micro SD card.
3. Turn the device back on.

Notes about Micro SD card use:

- If the device has a problem identifying the inserted Micro SD card, turn off the device, remove the card, then reinsert it.
- Always power off the device before removing or inserting the memory card.
- Do not reset the device while a memory card is inserted.

# 15. Taking care of the E-Reader

This E-Reader is designed to be light, compact, and durable. However, it is an electronic device and must be handled carefully.

Unnecessary pressure or impact can damage the device. To avoid damage:

- Keep the device covered when not in use to protect the screen from scratches and other damage.
- Do not drop, crush, bend, or apply excessive force to the device.
- Do not expose the device to moisture, extreme temperatures, or harmful conditions.
- Clean the device by wiping it with a soft, dry cloth. Do not use harsh chemicals.

section_title: 16. Maintenance, repair, firmware upgrade, and operating environment
section_path: 16. Maintenance, repair, firmware upgrade, and operating environment
text:
# 16. Maintenance, repair, firmware upgrade, and operating environment

Do not attempt to repair or disassemble this reader. Contact the manufacturer if any of the following occurs:

1. Liquid is spilled on the device or foreign objects enter the device.
2. The device becomes wet from rain or water.
3. The device is damaged by falling.
4. The device shows obvious overheating.
5. The product still cannot work properly after correct operation.

Firmware upgrade:

If a firmware upgrade is needed in the future, firmware will be uploaded to the manufacturer’s website. You can also download the user manual and other instructions related to this E-Reader.

Proper operating environment:

The appropriate operating temperature for this device is 32–120 °F (0–50 °C). Beyond this temperature range, screen display quality may deteriorate. Avoid using the device outdoors in winter if the temperature is outside the recommended range.

Do not place the device in environments with moisture, dust, or high temperature.

Avoid impact and pressure:

Do not shake, squeeze, or impact the device severely. Avoid applying excessive pressure to the screen or device body. For better protection, keep the device in the leather case provided in the package.

Avoid inserting objects into the device:

Do not place any object into gaps or openings on the device. These openings provide ventilation and heat dissipation and must not be blocked or covered.

# 17. Technical specifications

- Size: 9.13 × 6 × 0.6 inches (201 × 132 × 12.8 mm)
- Weight: 0.40 lb (170 g), battery included
- Screen size: 7-inch TFT color LCD
- Resolution: 800 × 480 pixels
- Storage memory: 32 MB RAM, 2 GB flash
- Processor: ARM 400 MHz
- Communication ports: USB client v2.0 Mini USB connector; Micro SD card slot
- Audio outputs: 3.5 mm stereo earphone jack; built-in speaker
- Battery: Rechargeable built-in lithium-polymer battery, 2000 mAh
- Peripherals: USB synchronization cable
- Operating system: Android
- Software suite: Multi-format eBook reader
- Supported image formats: JPG, GIF, PNG
- Supported sound formats: WAV, WMA, MP3
- Supported video formats: AVI, RMVB, MOV, MP4
- Supported text formats: TXT, EPUB, FB2, PDF, HTML
- Power source: 5 V, 2 A
- Power consumption: < 5 W

# 18. Troubleshooting

Problem: The e-book reader cannot power on.

- Charge the device until the power indicator bar is full.
- If the device is defective, contact the manufacturer for instructions.

Problem: The device cannot be charged.

- The AC adaptor may be defective. Contact the manufacturer for a replacement.
- The USB cable may be defective. Contact the manufacturer for a replacement.

Problem: There is no sound or there is noise when using earphones.

- Adjust the volume setting and make sure the volume is not set to 0.
- Try another pair of earphones.
- Make sure the music file compression quality is sufficient. Low-quality music files may cause noise and distortion.

Problem: Files cannot be downloaded to the reader.

- The USB cable may be defective.
- The E-Reader memory may be full.
- Windows 98 may require a USB 2.0 driver to detect the e-book reader as a removable disk.

Problem: Music files cannot be played.

- The reader can play many popular audio formats, but some newer music formats or resolutions may not work properly on this device. Contact the manufacturer’s technical support for assistance.

# 1. Safety warnings

Color Television Owner's Manual

WARNING: To reduce the risk of fire or electric shock, do not expose this product to rain or moisture.

CAUTION: To reduce the risk of electric shock, do not remove the cover or back. There are no user-serviceable parts inside. Refer servicing to qualified service personnel.

# 2. Clean the television safely

Unplug the television receiver from the wall outlet before cleaning.

Use a damp cloth for cleaning. Do not use liquid cleaners or aerosol cleaners.

Do not use attachments that are not recommended by the television receiver manufacturer, as they may cause hazards.

# 3. Use the correct power supply

Operate this television receiver only from the type of power source indicated on the marking label.

If you are not sure what type of power is supplied to your home, consult your television dealer or local power company.

# 4. Install the television safely

Do not use this television receiver near water, such as near a bathtub, washbowl, kitchen sink, laundry tub, wet basement, or swimming pool.

Do not place the television receiver on an unstable cart, stand, or table. The television receiver may fall, causing serious injury to a child or adult and serious damage to the appliance.

Use only a cart or stand recommended by the manufacturer or sold with the television receiver. Wall or shelf mounting should follow the manufacturer's instructions and should use a mounting kit approved by the manufacturer.

Slots and openings in the cabinet and on the back or bottom are provided for ventilation. These openings help ensure reliable operation and protect the television receiver from overheating. Do not block or cover these openings. Never place the television receiver on a bed, sofa, rug, or similar surface where the ventilation openings may be blocked.

Do not place this television receiver in a built-in installation, such as a bookcase, unless proper ventilation is provided.

It is recommended not to operate this unit near speakers or large metallic furniture, as magnetism may disturb color purity or uniformity on the screen.

Wet location marking: The apparatus must not be exposed to dripping or splashing. Do not place objects filled with liquids, such as vases, on the apparatus.

section_title: 5. Use and service the television safely
section_path: 5. Use and service the television safely
text:
# 5. Use and service the television safely

Do not allow anything to rest on the power cord. Do not place the television receiver where people may walk on or damage the cord.

Do not overload wall outlets or extension cords, as this can result in fire or electric shock.

Never push objects of any kind into the television receiver through cabinet slots. Objects may touch dangerous voltage points or short out parts, which could result in fire or electric shock.

Never spill liquid of any kind on the television receiver.

Do not attempt to service this television yourself. Opening or removing covers may expose you to dangerous voltage or other hazards. Refer all servicing to qualified service personnel.

section_title: 6. Record the model and serial numbers
section_path: 6. Record the model and serial numbers
text:
# 6. Record the model and serial numbers

The serial number and model number are found on the back of the unit. The serial number is unique to this unit.

Record the requested information and retain this guide as a permanent record of your purchase. Keep your purchase receipt as proof of purchase.

# 7. Use the remote control buttons

The following buttons may be available on the remote control, depending on the model.

[Manual35_0]

1. POWER or ON/OFF: Turns the TV on or off. See "Turning on/off the TV".
2. NUMBER buttons: Select a channel directly.
3. APC (Auto Picture Control): Selects factory preset picture modes according to the viewing environment.
4. MENU: Displays on-screen menus.
5. CHANNEL UP/DOWN (CH ▲/▼): Selects channels or menu items.
6. VOLUME UP/DOWN (VOL ◄/►): Adjusts volume or changes the selected menu setting.
7. ENTER (OK): Exits the displayed menu, memorizes an adjusted setting, or recalls the current TV mode when using the remote control.
8. FCR (Favorite Channel Review): Selects favorite channels.
9. AUTO PRG. (Auto Program): Memorizes channels automatically.
10. EYE / *: Switches the Eye picture function on or off on some models. The * key has no function.
11. REVIEW: Returns to the previous channel on some models.
12. WIDE / ZOOM / *: Selects the picture format, such as 4:3, 16:9, or ZOOM, on some models. The * key has no function.
13. MUTE: Mutes the sound. Press again to restore the sound.
14. TV/VIDEO: Selects TV, VIDEO, or COMPONENT mode.
15. CAPTION: Selects the caption mode on some models.
16. SLEEP: Sets the sleep timer.
17. MEMORY/ERASE: Memorizes or erases a selected channel on some models.
18. PICTURE: Displays picture modes one by one.
19. MTS: Selects MTS sound on some models.
20. TURBO SOUND / TURBO-S: Switches the Turbo Sound function on or off on some models.
21. TURBO PICTURE / TURBO-P: Switches the Turbo Picture function on or off on some models.

[Manual35_1]

[Manual35_2]

Remote control battery note: Open the battery compartment cover on the back of the remote control and insert the batteries with the correct polarity. Use two 1.5 V AAA batteries. Do not mix used batteries with new batteries.

# 8. Identify the front panel controls

This is a simplified representation of the front panel. The actual controls may vary by model.

[Manual35_3]

1. STANDBY indicator: Illuminates red when the TV is in standby mode.
2. Remote control sensor: Receives signals from the remote control.
3. Eye sensor: Adjusts the picture according to surrounding conditions on some models.

# 9. Prepare the TV before operation

Before operating the TV, make sure the following steps have been completed:

1. Connect the TV to an antenna or cable system.
2. Plug the TV into a power outlet.
3. Note that the on-screen display shown in this manual may differ from your TV. The images are examples to help explain operation.

section_title: 10. Turn the TV on or off
section_path: 10. Turn the TV on or off
text:
# 10. Turn the TV on or off

Press the POWER or ON/OFF button on the TV. The TV switches to standby mode and the standby indicator lights red.

To switch the TV on from standby mode, press TV/VIDEO or CH ▲/▼ on the TV, or press POWER, TV/VIDEO, CH ▲/▼, or a number button on the remote control. A channel number appears on the screen. The on-screen display disappears after a few seconds.

To return the TV to standby mode, press the POWER button on the remote control.

To switch the TV off completely, press the POWER button on the TV.

# 11. Select the on-screen language

1. Press MENU.
2. Press CH ▲/▼ until the language menu is displayed.
3. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select Language.
4. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select the desired language.
5. From this point on, the on-screen display is shown in the selected language.
6. Press MENU repeatedly to exit.

[Manual35_4]

section_title: 12. Memorize channels automatically with the AUTO PRG button
section_path: 12. Memorize channels automatically with the AUTO PRG button
text:
# 12. Memorize channels automatically with the AUTO PRG button

Use channel memorization before selecting channels normally. There are two ways to memorize channels: AUTO PROGRAM and MANUAL PROGRAM.

AUTO PROGRAM searches for and memorizes active channels in ascending order. If there are additional channels that you want to add or delete, use MANUAL PROGRAM.

To use the AUTO PRG button:

1. Press AUTO PRG. on the remote control.
2. Press AUTO PRG. again, or use the on-screen selection to start AUTO PROGRAM.
3. The TV searches and memorizes active channels.
4. To stop auto programming, press ENTER (OK). Only the channels found up to that point are memorized.

[Manual35_5]

Notes:

- If the programmed signal has poor quality, run Auto Program again.
- AUTO PROGRAM stores all receivable channels, including RF and cable channels.
- If general wireless TV channels and cable TV channels are duplicated, use the number buttons 0-9 to select the desired channel.

[Manual35_6]
[Manual35_6 description: The figure consists of two arranged horizontally rectangular, middle through/by a arrow connection. left side rectangular inside text is "Channels of general wireless TV". right side rectangular inside text is "Channels of Cable TV". middle arrow is black, points to two left and right, connection two rectangular.]

[Manual35_7]

section_title: 13. Memorize channels automatically from the menu
section_path: 13. Memorize channels automatically from the menu
text:
# 13. Memorize channels automatically from the menu

1. Press MENU.
2. Press CH ▲/▼ until the channel menu is displayed.
3. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select Auto Program.
4. Press VOL ► to enter Auto Program mode.
5. AUTO PROGRAM starts.

[Manual35_8]

# 14. Memorize or erase channels manually

You can manually memorize or erase a selected channel.

Using the MEMORY/ERASE button:

1. Press CH ▲/▼ or the number buttons to select the channel number you want to memorize or erase.
2. Press MEMORY/ERASE to select Memory or Erase.
3. The on-screen display appears and confirms the selection.

[Manual35_9]

Using the menu:

1. Press MENU.
2. Press CH ▲/▼ until the channel menu is displayed.
3. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select Manual.
4. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select Channel.
5. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select the channel number you want to memorize or erase.

[Manual35_10]

6. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select Memory.

[Manual35_11]

7. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select On or Off.
8. Press MENU repeatedly to exit.

# 15. Select channels and adjust volume

To select a channel, press CH ▲/▼ to move to the upper or lower channel, or press the number buttons to select the desired channel directly.

To increase the volume, press VOL ►. To decrease the volume, press VOL ◄.

To mute the sound, press MUTE. The word "Mute" appears on the screen. This is convenient when receiving telephone calls. To restore sound, press MUTE again or press VOL ◄/►.

[Manual35_12]

[Manual35_13]

# 16. Set the clock

Set the current time before setting the On Timer or Off Timer.

1. Press MENU.
2. Press CH ▲/▼ until the time menu is displayed.
3. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select Clock.
4. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to adjust the hour.
5. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to adjust the minute.
6. Press MENU repeatedly to exit.

[Manual35_14]

# 17. Set the Off Timer

The Off Timer automatically switches the TV to standby mode at a preset time.

1. Press MENU.
2. Press CH ▲/▼ until the time menu is displayed.
3. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select Off Timer.
4. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to adjust the hour.
5. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to adjust the minute.
6. Select On to activate the timer, or Off to deactivate it.
7. Press MENU repeatedly to exit.

[Manual35_15]

Note: If the same time is set for the On Timer and Off Timer, only the Off Timer operates.

# 18. Set the On Timer

The On Timer automatically turns the TV on at a preset time and channel.

1. Press MENU.
2. Press CH ▲/▼ until the time menu is displayed.
3. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select On Timer.
4. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to adjust the hour.
5. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to adjust the minute.
6. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select the desired channel from memorized channels.
7. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to adjust the desired volume level.
8. Select On to activate the timer, or Off to deactivate it.
9. Press MENU repeatedly to exit.

[Manual35_16]

Notes:

- If no button is pressed within 2 hours after the TV is turned on by the On Timer, the TV automatically switches back to standby mode.
- The TV must be in standby mode for the On Timer to work.

# 19. Set the Sleep Timer

The Sleep Timer automatically turns the TV off after the selected time elapses.

Press SLEEP repeatedly to select the desired sleep time. Each press changes the sleep time in this sequence:

10 → 20 → 30 → 60 → 90 → 120 → 180 → 240 minutes → Off

[Manual35_17]

Notes:

- After a few seconds, the selected sleep time disappears from the screen and starts automatically.
- To view the remaining sleep time, press SLEEP once.
- To cancel the sleep timer, press SLEEP until the Sleep setting is set to Off or "---".

# 20. Set Auto Off

If there is no input signal, the TV automatically switches to standby mode after 10 minutes.

1. Press MENU.
2. Press CH ▲/▼ until the special menu is displayed.
3. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select Auto Off.
4. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select On or Off.
5. Press MENU repeatedly to exit.

[Manual35_18]

section_title: 23. Use Auto Demonstration on supported models
section_path: 23. Use Auto Demonstration on supported models
text:

Auto Demonstration lets you review all menus programmed in the TV.

1. Press MENU.
2. Press CH ▲/▼ until the special menu is displayed.
3. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select Auto Demo.

1. Press MENU.
2. Press CH ▲/▼ until the channel menu is displayed.
3. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select Favorite.

[Manual35_22]

Fine tuning adjusts the picture when reception is poor, such as when the image has horizontal stripes, is twisted, or has no color.

1. Press MENU.
2. Press CH ▲/▼ until the channel menu is displayed.
3. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select Manual.

Notes:

- To release the memorized fine tuning, program the fine-tuned channel again by AUTO PROGRAM or MANUAL PROGRAM.

[Manual35_24]

section_title: 31. Understand closed captions and reception issues
section_path: 31. Understand closed captions and reception issues
text:
# 31. Understand closed captions and reception issues

Closed captioning converts the audio portion of a television program into written words that appear on the television screen, similar to subtitles. Closed captions let viewers read the dialogue and narration of television programs.

Captions are subtitles of program dialogue and narration. For prerecorded programs, captions can be prepared in advance. Live programs can be captioned by real-time captioning, which is normally performed by professional reporters using a shorthand machine and computer translation.

Captioning is useful for hearing-impaired viewers and may also help with language learning.

[Manual35_36]

Caption tips:

- Not all TV broadcasts include closed caption signals.
- Some TV stations broadcast two different caption signals on the same channel. Select Mode 1 or Mode 2 to choose which signal to view. Mode 1 is usually the signal with captions, while Mode 2 may show demonstration or programming information.
- Your TV may not receive caption signals normally under poor reception conditions.

Examples of poor reception conditions:

[television0_01]

Ignition interference: The picture may flutter, drift, show black spots, or show horizontal streaking. This is usually caused by interference from automobile ignition systems, neon lamps, electrical drills, or other electrical appliances.

[television0_02]

Ghosts: Ghosts occur when the TV signal splits and follows two paths: a direct path and a reflected path from tall buildings, hills, or other objects. Changing the direction or position of the antenna may improve reception.

[television0_03]

Snow: If the receiver is located in a weak or fringe signal area, the picture may be marred by small dots. A special antenna may be necessary to improve the picture.

Other causes include an old, bad, or illegally recorded tape; strong random signals from a car or airplane; a weak antenna signal; or a program that was not captioned when produced, transmitted, or taped.

# 32. Use caption and text functions

Text services provide information on many subjects, such as captioned program lists, weather forecasts, stock exchange topics, and news for hearing-impaired viewers, through the full TV screen. Not all stations offer text services, even if they offer captioning.

Note: If the TV receives a poor signal, an empty black box may appear and disappear even when text mode is selected. This is normal under poor signal conditions.

Using the CAPTION button:

1. Press CAPTION.
2. Press CAPTION repeatedly to select OFF, Mode 1, Mode 2, Text 1, or Text 2.
3. Press ENTER (OK) to exit.

[Manual35_37]

Using the menu:

1. Press MENU.
2. Press CH ▲/▼ to select the Special menu.
3. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select Caption.
4. Press VOL ►, and then press CH ▲/▼ to select Off, Mode 1, Mode 2, Text 1, or Text 2.
5. Press MENU repeatedly to exit.

[Manual35_38]

Note: The TV remembers the last caption mode setting even after the TV is turned off.

[Manual35_39]

# 34. Identify external equipment jacks on supported models

You can connect additional equipment, such as VCRs and camcorders, to the TV. The jack layout shown is an example and may differ from your TV.

1. IN 1 jacks: Connect external equipment outputs, such as VCR, laser disc, or camcorder outputs, to these inputs. Press TV/VIDEO to select VIDEO 1.
2. IN 2 jacks: Connect external equipment outputs, such as VCR, laser disc, or camcorder outputs, to these inputs. Press TV/VIDEO to select VIDEO 2 or S-VIDEO.
3. OUT jacks: Connect external equipment inputs, such as VCR or audio amplifier inputs, to these outputs for recording or monitoring the selected program.
4. Earphone jack on some models: This jack may be located on the front or side of the TV.

Note: The TV remembers the last input mode setting even after the TV is turned off.

[Manual35_41]

section_title: 35. Connect a VCR or S-VHS VCR
section_path: 35. Connect a VCR or S-VHS VCR
text:
# 35. Connect a VCR or S-VHS VCR

To connect audio/video input jacks:

1. Connect the audio/video output jacks of the VCR to the IN 1 (A/V) jacks on the side or back of the TV. If you connect only the audio jack, sound from the TV may not be heard correctly.
2. Press TV/VIDEO to select VIDEO 1.
3. Press PLAY on the VCR. The video playback appears on the TV screen.

[Manual35_42]

Notes:

- On some stereo models, if you connect the VCR audio/video output jacks to the IN 2 (A/V) jacks on the front or side of the TV, select VIDEO 2.
- For a mono VCR, connect the VCR audio output jack to the AUDIO L/MONO IN jack of the TV so the sound can be heard from both speakers. If you connect it to the AUDIO R IN jack, sound is heard only from the right speaker.
- On some mono models, when input jacks on the front panel and back panel are connected to external equipment at the same time, the front panel input jacks have priority.

To connect an S-VHS VCR on supported models:

1. Connect the S-VHS output jack of the VCR to the S-VIDEO jack on the side or back of the TV.
2. Connect the audio/video output jacks of the VCR to the IN 2 (A/V) jacks on the front or side of the TV.
3. Press TV/VIDEO to select S-VIDEO.
4. Press PLAY on the VCR. The video playback appears on the TV screen.

[television0_04]

section_title: 36. Record with a VCR on supported models
section_path: 36. Record with a VCR on supported models
text:
# 36. Record with a VCR on supported models

To record a TV program:

1. Connect the audio/video input jacks of the recording VCR to the OUT (A/V) jacks on the back of the TV.
2. Select the program number on the TV.
3. Set the recording VCR to record.

[television0_05]

To record a program from other connected equipment:

1. Connect the output jacks of the playback VCR to the IN 1 (A/V) jacks on the side or back of the TV.
2. Connect the input jacks of the recording VCR to the OUT (A/V) jacks on the back of the TV.
3. Press TV/VIDEO to select VIDEO 1. If the playback device is connected to the IN 2 (A/V) jacks on the side of the TV, select VIDEO 2.
4. Press PLAY on the playback VCR and set the recording VCR to record.

[television0_06]

# 1. XL490/XL495 cordless landline phone overview

[landline_01]

This manual applies to the XL490 and XL495 cordless landline phone models. The XL495 includes an answering machine; functions marked “XL495 only” are available only on that model.

Use this manual to set up the base station, charge and configure the handset, make and manage calls, maintain the phonebook and call lists, configure handset settings, use the answering machine, and troubleshoot common issues.

# 2. Important safety instructions

Follow these safety instructions before using the phone.

- Handsfree activation can suddenly increase the earpiece volume to a very high level. Keep the handset away from your ear when handsfree mode is activated.
- This equipment cannot make emergency calls during a power failure. Make alternative arrangements for emergency calls.
- Do not allow the product to come into contact with liquids.
- Do not use cleaning agents containing alcohol, ammonia, benzene, or abrasives.
- Do not expose the phone to excessive heat from heating equipment or direct sunlight.
- Do not drop the phone or allow objects to fall on it.
- Active mobile phones nearby may cause interference.

[Manual22_0]

Power requirements:

- The product requires a 100–240 V AC electrical supply.
- Communication can be lost during a power failure.
- The voltage on the telephone network is classified as TNV-3, as defined in EN 60950.

Operating and storage temperatures:

- Operate the phone where the temperature is between 0 °C and +40 °C, with up to 90% relative humidity.
- Store the phone where the temperature is between -20 °C and +45 °C, with up to 95% relative humidity.
- Battery life may be shorter at low temperatures.

Warning: The electrical network is classified as hazardous. The only way to power down the charger is to unplug the power supply from the electrical outlet. Make sure the outlet is always easily accessible.

[Manual22_1]

To avoid damage or malfunction:

- Use only the power supply listed in the user instructions.
- Use only the batteries listed in the user instructions.
- Replacing the battery with an incorrect type can cause an explosion risk.
- Dispose of used batteries according to the instructions.
- Do not dispose of batteries in fire.
- Always use the cables supplied with the product.
- Do not allow charging contacts or batteries to touch metal objects.
- Do not let small metal objects touch the product, as this can reduce audio quality or damage the product.
- Metallic objects may be retained if placed near or on the handset receiver.
- Do not use the product where there are explosive hazards.
- Do not open the handset, base station, or charger, as high voltage may be present.
- For pluggable equipment, the socket outlet must be installed near the equipment and must be easily accessible.

# 3. Package contents

Check that the package includes the correct items.

[Manual22_2]

Base station for XL490.

[Manual22_3]

Base station for XL495.

[Manual22_4]

Power adapter.

[Manual22_5]

Line cord.

[Manual22_6]

Quick start guide.

Note: In some countries, the line adapter must be connected to the line cord before the line cord is plugged into the telephone socket.

Tip: In multi-handset packs, additional handsets, chargers, and power adapters are included.

# 4. Handset controls and indicators

[Manual22_7]

[Manual22_8]

The handset includes the following controls and indicators.

- Earpiece: Used for listening during handset calls.
- Navigation up key: Scrolls up in menus, increases earpiece or speaker volume, and opens the phonebook in standby mode.
- Clear/Back key: Deletes text or digits, cancels an operation, opens the redial list in standby mode, and changes the sound profile during a call.
- End key: Ends a call, exits a menu or operation, and switches the handset on or off when pressed and held.

[Manual22_9]

- m1/m2/m3 keys: Store emergency numbers or frequently used numbers.

[Manual22_10]

- Space/Key lock key: Enters a space during text editing and locks or unlocks the keypad in standby mode when pressed and held.
- Pause key: Enters a pause when making a call if pressed and held.
- Uppercase/lowercase key: Switches between uppercase and lowercase during text editing.
- Mute/Answering machine key: Mutes or unmutes the microphone. On XL495, it opens the answering machine menu in standby mode and can be used to listen to new answering machine messages.
- Microphone: Picks up your voice.
- Audio boost key: Activates or deactivates audio boost in earpiece or handsfree mode.
- Speaker key: Turns the speakerphone on or off and lets you make or receive calls through the speaker.

[Manual22_11]

- Intercom key: Press and hold to make an intercom call on multi-handset versions. It can also change dial mode from pulse to temporary tone mode.
- Navigation down key: Scrolls down in menus, decreases earpiece or speaker volume, and opens the call log in standby mode.

[Manual22_12]

- Call/Recall key: Makes and receives calls. The recall function is network dependent.

[Manual22_13]

- Menu/OK key: Opens the main menu in standby mode, confirms a selection, opens the options menu, and selects the function shown directly above the key on the handset screen.
- LED indicator: Shows events or charging status.
- Loudspeaker: Plays speakerphone audio and other sounds.
- Battery door: Covers the rechargeable batteries.

[Manual22_14]

section_title: 5. Base station controls and answering machine controls
section_path: 5. Base station controls and answering machine controls
text:
# 5. Base station controls and answering machine controls

[Manual22_15]

[Manual22_16]

On the XL495 base station, use the answering machine controls as follows:

- Answering machine on/off key: Turns the answering machine on or off.
- Delete key: Deletes the current playback message. Press and hold to delete all old messages.
- Volume down/up keys: Decrease or increase the speaker volume.
- Skip backward/forward keys: Skip backward or forward during playback.
- Play/Stop key: Plays messages or stops message playback.

Base station paging and registration:

[Manual22_18]

[Manual22_19]

- Press the paging key to find handsets.
- Press and hold the paging key to enter registration mode.
- The base station includes a speaker for message playback and alerts.

# 6. Connect the base station

[Manual22_20]

Caution: Read the safety instructions before connecting and installing the handset.

[Manual22_21]

Warning: Make sure the power supply voltage matches the voltage printed on the back or underside of the phone. Use only the supplied power adapter to charge the batteries.

Note: If you subscribe to DSL high-speed internet service through the telephone line, install a DSL filter between the telephone line cord and the power socket. The filter helps prevent noise and caller ID problems caused by DSL interference. Contact your DSL service provider for more information. The type plate is located on the bottom of the base station.

[Manual22_22]

To connect the base station:

1. Connect one end of the power adapter to the DC input jack on the bottom of the base station.
2. Connect the other end of the power adapter to a wall power socket.
3. Connect one end of the line cord to the telephone socket on the bottom of the base station.
4. Connect the other end of the line cord to the telephone wall socket.

# 7. Install and charge the handset

The batteries are pre-installed in the handset. Pull the battery tape from the battery door before charging.

[Manual22_23]

[Manual22_24]

Caution:

- Keep batteries away from heat, sunlight, and fire.
- Never discard batteries in fire.
- Use only the supplied batteries.
- Do not mix batteries of different brands or types.

[Manual22_25]

Charge the batteries for 8 hours before first use. If the handset becomes warm during charging, this is normal.

Warning: Check the battery polarity when inserting batteries. Incorrect polarity may damage the product.

[Manual22_27]

To charge the handset:

1. Place the handset on the base station or charger.
2. When the handset is correctly placed, you hear a docking sound.
3. The handset begins charging.

You can activate or deactivate the docking tone in the sound settings. After charging, the phone is ready to use.

section_title: 8. Configure the phone for first use
section_path: 8. Configure the phone for first use
text:
# 8. Configure the phone for first use

When you use the phone for the first time, a welcome message may appear.

1. Press [OK].
2. Select your country or language, then press [OK] to confirm.

Note: The country/language setting is country dependent. If no welcome message appears, the setting is already preset for your country. You can then set the date and time.

To reset the display language later:

1. Select [Menu] > [Phone setup] > [Language], then press [OK].
2. Select a language, then press [OK].
3. The setting is saved.

To set the date and time:

1. Select [Menu] > [Phone setup] > [Date & time], then press [OK].
2. Enter the date with the numeric keys, then press [OK].
3. Enter the time with the numeric keys.
4. If the time uses 12-hour format, press the navigation keys to select [am] or [pm]. This option is country dependent.
5. Press [OK] to confirm.

section_title: 9. Change the remote access PIN code on XL495
section_path: 9. Change the remote access PIN code on XL495
text:
# 9. Change the remote access PIN code on XL495

[Manual22_26]

This feature is available only for models with an answering machine. The default remote access PIN code is 0000. Change it to improve security.

To change the remote access PIN:

1. Select [Menu] > [Answ. Machine] > [Remote access] > [Change PIN], then press [OK].
2. Enter the old PIN, then press [OK].
3. Enter the new PIN code, then press [OK].
4. Enter the new PIN code again, then press [Save].
5. The setting is saved.
