# 5. Mount the camera on a drop-ceiling T-rail

To mount the camera on a drop-ceiling T-rail, use the included hardware. The hardware can be used to mount to most 9/16 inch, 15/16 inch, or 1-1/2 inch T-rails.

1. Using the dashed lines on the mount plate template as a guide, set the proper spacing of the clips.

[Manual33_10]

2. Tighten the set screws on the T-rail clips and secure them using a 5/64 inch (2 mm) hex key.

[Manual33_11]

3. Attach the mount plate to the T-rail clips using the mount plate holes marked with the letter `G`.

[Manual33_12]

4. Attach the T-rail clips to the T-rail by rotating them and snapping them into place as shown. The black foam pads should be compressed slightly after installation.

[Manual33_13]

Standard T-rail screws: 6-32 × 4 mm.

[Manual33_14]

For recessed T-rails, follow the modification guidance shown in the installation illustration.

# 6. Power the camera

Remove the cable guard and route the Ethernet cable from an active port on an 802.3af PoE switch or PoE injector to the camera.

Note: Power over Ethernet supports a maximum cable length of 300 ft (100 m).

# 7. Interpret the LED indicator

The camera has an LED light on the front of the unit that indicates system functionality and performance.

Flashing green at a 2-second interval means the camera is upgrading or initializing for the first time.

Solid green means the camera is operating normally.

section_title: 1. Outdoor gas grill overview and emergency gas warning
section_path: 1. Outdoor gas grill overview and emergency gas warning
text:
# 1. Outdoor gas grill overview and emergency gas warning

This use and care guide is for an outdoor LP gas grill. Read and follow all safety, assembly, use, and care instructions before assembling or cooking with the grill. Failure to follow the instructions may lead to fire or explosion, which could result in property damage, personal injury, or death.

[Manual19_0]

Tools needed for assembly include an adjustable wrench, screwdriver, and 7/16 inch combination wrench. These tools are not provided.

[Manual19_1]

If you smell gas:

1. Shut off gas to the appliance.
2. Extinguish any open flame.
3. Open the lid.
4. If the odor continues, keep away from the appliance and immediately call your gas supplier or fire department.

[Manual19_2]

Do not store or use gasoline or other flammable liquids or vapors near this or any other appliance. Do not store an LP tank that is not connected for use near this or any other appliance.

For help with assembly or replacement parts, call the grill service center. Record the model number, serial number, and date purchased from the rating label on the grill. The installer or assembler should leave these instructions with the consumer, and the consumer should keep the manual for future reference.

[Manual19_3]

Some parts may contain sharp edges. Wear protective gloves if necessary.

[Manual19_4]

This grill is for residential use only. Do not use it for commercial cooking.

[Manual19_5]

section_title: 2. Installation safety, California Proposition 65, and safety symbols
section_path: 2. Installation safety, California Proposition 65, and safety symbols
text:
# 2. Installation safety, California Proposition 65, and safety symbols

California Proposition 65 warning: combustion by-products produced when using this product contain chemicals known to the State of California to cause cancer, birth defects, and other reproductive harm.

Installation safety precautions:

1. Use the grill, as purchased, only with LP propane gas and the regulator/valve assembly supplied.
2. Grill installation must conform with local codes. In the absence of local codes, installation must conform with applicable fuel gas, propane storage, recreational vehicle, or related codes.
3. Electrical accessories, such as a rotisserie or light, must be electrically grounded according to local codes or the National Electrical Code / Canadian Electrical Code.
4. Keep electrical cords and fuel supply hoses away from hot surfaces.
5. Do not use this grill in or on recreational vehicles or boats.
6. This grill is safety certified for use only in the United States and/or Canada. Do not modify it for use in another location.

Safety symbols used in this manual:

[Manual19_6]

Danger indicates an imminently hazardous situation which, if not avoided, will result in death or serious injury.

[Manual19_7]

Warning means you must be alert to the possibility of serious bodily injury if instructions are not followed.

[Manual19_8]

Caution indicates a potentially hazardous situation which, if not avoided, may result in minor or moderate injury.

section_title: 3. Repair protection agreement, warranty, and installation service
section_path: 3. Repair protection agreement, warranty, and installation service
text:
# 3. Repair protection agreement, warranty, and installation service

The repair protection agreement provides access to professional repair service, covered repairs, discounts on service and preventive maintenance, and phone support. Some limitations and exclusions apply.

Kenmore grill warranty:

1. One-year full warranty: if the grill fails due to a defect in material or workmanship within one year from the purchase date, call for free repair or replacement if repair is not possible.
2. Ten-year limited warranty on burners: for ten years from the purchase date, any burner that rusts through will be replaced free of charge. After the first year, labor for installation is the owner’s responsibility.

Warranty coverage excludes ignitor batteries, grill paint loss, discoloration, rusting, normal wear, accident, improper maintenance, commercial use, and rental use. Warranty coverage applies only if the grill is used in the United States.

For Sears professional installation of home appliances and other major home items in the United States or Canada, call the listed service number.

section_title: 4. LP tank safety, storage, and transport
section_path: 4. LP tank safety, storage, and transport
text:
# 4. LP tank safety, storage, and transport

Never store a spare LP cylinder under or near the appliance or in an enclosed area.

[Manual19_9]

[Manual19_10]

Never fill an LP cylinder more than 80% full. An overfilled or improperly stored cylinder is hazardous because gas may release from the safety relief valve, causing an intense fire with risk of property damage, serious injury, or death. If you see, smell, or hear gas escaping, immediately move away from the LP cylinder or appliance and call the fire department.

To remove, transport, and store the LP tank:

1. Turn all control knobs and the LP tank valve to OFF.
2. Turn the coupling nut counterclockwise by hand only. Do not use tools.
3. Lift the LP tank wire upward off the LP tank collar.
4. Lift the LP tank up and off the support bracket.
5. Install the safety cap onto the LP tank valve.
6. Always use the cap and strap supplied with the valve.

[Manual19_11]

A disconnected LP tank in storage or transport must have the safety cap installed. Do not store an LP tank in enclosed spaces such as a carport, garage, porch, covered patio, other building, or overheated vehicle. Do not store an LP tank where children play.

section_title: 5. LP tank requirements, filling, and exchange
section_path: 5. LP tank requirements, filling, and exchange
text:
# 5. LP tank requirements, filling, and exchange

The LP tank used with this grill must meet these requirements:

1. Use only an LP tank measuring 12 inches (30.5 cm) in diameter by 18 inches (45.7 cm) tall, with a maximum capacity of 20 lb (9 kg).
2. The LP tank must be constructed and marked according to U.S. Department of Transportation or Canadian transport specifications.
3. The LP tank valve must have a Type 1 outlet compatible with the regulator or grill.
4. The tank must have a safety relief valve and a UL-listed Overfill Protection Device (OPD).

[Manual19_12]

The OPD feature is identified by a unique triangular hand wheel. Use only LP tanks equipped with this type of valve.

[Manual19_13]

The LP tank must be arranged for vapor withdrawal and must include a collar to protect the LP tank valve. Always keep LP tanks upright during use, transit, and storage.

LP gas is nontoxic, odorless, and colorless when produced. For safety, LP gas has been given an odor similar to rotten cabbage so it can be smelled. LP gas is highly flammable and may ignite unexpectedly when mixed with air.

When filling an LP tank:

1. Use only licensed and experienced LP dealers.
2. The LP dealer must purge a new tank before filling.
3. The dealer should never fill an LP tank more than 80% of tank volume.
4. A frosty regulator indicates gas overfill. Immediately close the LP tank valve and call a local LP gas dealer for assistance.
5. Do not release liquid propane gas into the atmosphere.

When exchanging an LP tank, use only reputable exchange companies that inspect, precision fill, test, and certify their tanks. Exchange your tank only for an OPD-equipped tank. Keep exchanged tanks upright during use, transit, and storage. Leak-test new and exchanged tanks before connecting them to the grill.

# 6. Leak-test the LP tank

Leak testing must be repeated each time the LP tank is exchanged or refilled.

For your safety:

1. Do not smoke during the leak test.
2. Do not use an open flame to check for gas leaks.
3. Leak-test the grill outdoors in a well-ventilated area, away from ignition sources such as gas-fired or electrical appliances.
4. During the leak test, keep the grill away from open flames or sparks.
5. Use a clean paintbrush and a 50/50 mild soap and water solution.
6. Brush the soapy solution onto the areas indicated in the figure. Leaks are indicated by growing bubbles.

[Manual19_14]

If growing bubbles appear, do not use or move the LP tank. Contact an LP gas supplier or your fire department.

Do not use household cleaning agents. They can damage gas train components.

[Manual19_15]

section_title: 7. Connect the regulator to the LP tank
section_path: 7. Connect the regulator to the LP tank
text:
# 7. Connect the regulator to the LP tank

To connect the regulator to the LP tank:

1. Make sure the LP tank is properly secured onto the grill.
2. Turn all control knobs to OFF.
3. Turn the LP tank OFF by turning the OPD hand wheel clockwise to a full stop.
4. Remove the protective cap from the LP tank valve. Always use the cap and strap supplied with the valve.

[Manual19_16]

Do not use a POL transport plug. It will defeat the safety feature of the valve.

[Manual19_17]

5. Hold the regulator and insert the nipple into the LP tank valve. Hand-tighten the coupling nut, keeping the regulator aligned straight with the LP tank valve to avoid cross-threading.

[Manual19_18]

6. Turn the coupling nut clockwise and tighten it to a full stop. The regulator will seal on the back-check feature in the LP tank valve, causing some resistance. An additional one-half to three-quarters turn is required to complete the connection. Tighten by hand only; do not use tools.

If you cannot complete the connection, disconnect the regulator and repeat steps 5 and 6. If you still cannot complete the connection, do not use this regulator.

[Manual19_19]

Do not insert tools or foreign objects into the valve outlet or safety relief valve. This may damage the valve and cause a leak. Leaking propane may result in explosion, fire, severe personal injury, or death. If a leak is detected at any time, stop and call the fire department. If you cannot stop a gas leak, immediately close the LP tank valve and call the LP gas supplier or fire department.

section_title: 8. Leak-test the valves, hose, and regulator
section_path: 8. Leak-test the valves, hose, and regulator
text:
# 8. Leak-test the valves, hose, and regulator

To leak-test the valves, hose, and regulator:

1. Turn all grill control knobs to OFF.
2. Make sure the regulator is tightly connected to the LP tank.
3. Completely open the LP tank valve by turning the OPD hand wheel counterclockwise. If you hear a rushing sound, turn the gas off immediately; there is a major leak at the connection. Correct the problem before proceeding.
4. Brush the soap-and-water solution onto the areas shown in the figure.

[Manual19_20]

5. If growing bubbles appear, there is a leak. Close the LP tank valve immediately and retighten connections. If leaks cannot be stopped, do not try to repair the grill. Call for replacement parts.
6. After the leak test, always close the LP tank valve by turning the hand wheel clockwise.

[Manual19_21]

Never attempt to attach this grill to the self-contained LP gas system of a camper trailer or motor home. Do not use the grill until it has been leak-tested.

[Manual19_22]

# 9. Use the grill safely

For safe use of the grill and to avoid serious injury:

1. Do not let children operate or play near the grill.
2. Keep the grill area clear and free from materials that burn.
3. Do not block holes in the bottom or back of the grill.
4. Check burner flames regularly.
5. Use the grill only in a well-ventilated outdoor space.
6. Never use the grill in an enclosed space such as a carport, garage, porch, covered patio, or under an overhead structure.
7. Do not use charcoal or ceramic briquettes in a gas grill unless briquettes are supplied with the grill.
8. Keep the grill at least 3 ft from any wall or surface.
9. Maintain 10 ft clearance from objects that can catch fire or ignition sources such as pilot lights and live electrical appliances.

[Manual19_23]

Safety tips:

1. Before opening the LP tank valve, check the coupling nut for tightness.
2. When the grill is not in use, turn off all control knobs and the LP tank valve.
3. Never move the grill while it is operating or still hot.
4. Use long-handled barbecue utensils and oven mitts to avoid burns and splatters.
5. Maximum load for shelves is 10 lb.
6. Do not use a cooking pot larger than 9 inches on the grid.
7. The grease tray must be installed in the opening in the back panel and should be emptied after each use. Do not remove the grease tray until the grill has completely cooled.
8. If grease or hot material drips from the grill onto the valve, hose, or regulator, turn off the gas supply at once. Determine the cause, correct it, then clean and inspect the valve, hose, and regulator before continuing. Perform a leak test.
9. The regulator may make a humming or whistling noise during operation. This does not affect safety or use.

[Manual19_24]

If the regulator frosts, turn off the grill and LP tank valve immediately. This indicates a problem with the tank; do not use that tank on any product. Return it to the supplier.

[Manual19_25]

If a burner does not light, turn the knobs to OFF, wait 5 minutes, and try again. Always close the valve during the 5-minute waiting period. If the burner does not ignite while the valve is open, gas will continue to flow out of the burner and could accidentally ignite.

Apartment dwellers should check with management to learn requirements and fire codes for using an LP gas grill in the apartment complex. If allowed, use the grill outside on the ground floor with a 3 ft clearance from walls or rails. Do not use the grill on or under balconies.

Never attempt to light a burner with the lid closed. A buildup of unignited gas inside a closed grill is hazardous. Never operate the grill with the LP tank out of the correct position specified in the assembly instructions. Always close the LP tank valve and remove the coupling nut before moving the LP tank from its specified operating position.

section_title: 10. Light the main burners with the ignitor or a match
section_path: 10. Light the main burners with the ignitor or a match
text:
# 10. Light the main burners with the ignitor or a match

Do not lean over the grill while lighting.

Ignitor lighting:

1. Open the lid during lighting.
2. Turn on the gas tank valve.
3. Push and turn a burner control knob to HI and immediately press and hold the electronic ignition button.
4. If ignition does not occur within 5 seconds, turn the burner control knob to OFF, wait 5 minutes, and repeat the lighting procedure.
5. Repeat these steps to light each burner individually.

Main burner match lighting:

1. Open the lid during lighting.
2. Place a match into the match holder hanging from the side of the cart.
3. Light the match and place it into the lighting hole on the right side of the firebox.
4. Push in and turn the right knob to HI. Make sure the burner lights and stays lit.
5. If ignition does not occur within 5 seconds, turn the burner control knob to OFF, wait 5 minutes for gas to clear, and repeat the lighting procedure.
6. Light the other burners by pushing each knob in and turning it to HI.
7. After lighting, leave the knobs in HI for 15 minutes to preheat the grill. Then turn the knobs to the desired cooking setting.

[Manual19_26]

Grease fire warning:

1. Closing the lid will not put out a grease fire. Grills are well ventilated for safety.
2. Do not use water on a grease fire; personal injury may result.
3. If a grease fire develops, turn the knobs and LP tank OFF.
4. Do not leave the grill unattended while preheating or burning off food residue on high.
5. If the grill has not been cleaned regularly, a grease fire can occur and damage the product.

[Manual19_27]

# 11. Light the side burner

Do not lean over the grill while lighting the side burner.

Side burner match lighting:

1. Open the lid during lighting.
2. Turn on the gas at the LP tank.
3. Place a lit match near the burner.
4. Turn the side burner knob to HI. Make sure the burner lights and stays lit.
5. If ignition does not occur within 5 seconds, turn the burner control knob to OFF, wait 5 minutes for gas to clear, and repeat the lighting procedure.

[Manual19_28]

section_title: 12. Prepare for the first cookout and perform routine checks
section_path: 12. Prepare for the first cookout and perform routine checks
text:
# 12. Prepare for the first cookout and perform routine checks

Before the first cookout, light the burners, make sure they are lit, close the lid, and warm up the grill on HIGH for 15 minutes. This cures the paint and parts and may produce an odor only during the first lighting.

Burner flame check:

Light the burner and rotate the knobs from HIGH to LOW. You should see a smaller flame in the LOW position than in the HIGH position. Always check the flame before each use. If only a low flame is seen, refer to the troubleshooting section for a sudden drop or low flame.

[Manual19_29]

Hose check:

Before each use, check whether hoses are cut, worn, or kinked. Replace damaged hoses before using the grill. Use only the valve/hose/regulator specified in the parts list.

[Manual19_30]

Turning the grill off:

1. Turn all knobs to OFF.
2. Turn the LP tank off by turning the OPD hand wheel clockwise to a full stop.

Ignitor check:

Turn gas off at the LP tank. Push and turn the burner control. Clicking should be heard and sparking should be seen each time between the collector box or burner and the electrodes. See troubleshooting if no click or spark occurs.

Valve check:

Make sure gas is off at the LP tank before checking valves. Knobs lock in the OFF position. To check valves, push in the knobs and release them; the knobs should spring back. If the knobs do not spring back, replace the valve assembly before using the grill. Turn knobs to LOW, then back to OFF. Valves should turn smoothly.

# 13. Clean the grill after use

General grill cleaning:

1. Keep the outside of the grill looking new by cleaning it once a month with warm soap and water or a non-abrasive cleaner.
2. If you do not have a grill cover, wipe off dust and grime before starting the grill.
3. Coat the cooking grids with spray-on cooking oil to help keep food from sticking and make cleanup easier.
4. After cooking, scrape the grates with a long-handled brass wire bristle brush.
5. Check the inside of the grill bottom for grease buildup and clean often, especially after cooking fatty meat.
6. Do not mistake brown or black grease and smoke accumulation for paint. Apply a strong detergent-and-water solution or use a grill cleaner with a scrub brush on the inside of the grill lid and bottom. Rinse and let it air dry completely. Do not apply caustic grill or oven cleaner to painted surfaces.
7. Wash plated wire grates with concentrated grill cleaner or a soap-and-water solution. Dry thoroughly and store indoors between cookouts.
8. Wash plastic parts with warm soapy water and wipe dry. Do not use citrus cleaner, abrasive cleaner, degreaser, or concentrated grill cleaner on plastic parts.
9. Clean porcelain grates with a baking soda/water solution or specially formulated cleaner. Use non-abrasive scouring powder for stubborn stains.
10. If a bristle brush is used on cooking surfaces, make sure no loose bristles remain on the surfaces before grilling. Do not clean cooking surfaces while the grill is hot.

section_title: 14. Prevent flashback and clean the burner assembly
section_path: 14. Prevent flashback and clean the burner assembly
text:
# 14. Prevent flashback and clean the burner assembly

Spider alert: if the grill becomes hard to light or the flame is not as strong as it should be, check and clean the burners.

[Manual19_31]

[Manual19_32]

Spiders or small insects may create flashback problems by spinning webs, building nests, and laying eggs in the grill burner tubes. This obstructs gas flow to the burner. Backed-up gas can ignite in the tube behind the control panel, damaging the grill and potentially causing injury. To prevent flashbacks and ensure good performance, remove and clean the burner assembly before use whenever the grill has been idle for an extended period.

To clean or replace parts of the burner assembly:

1. Turn gas off at the control knobs and LP cylinder.
2. Remove cooking grates and flame tamers.
3. Remove hitch pins and carryover tubes from the rear of the burners.
4. Remove the hitch pin to disengage the burner from the bracket on the firebox.
5. Detach the electrode from the burner with a flat screwdriver by pressing the electrode clamp out of the burner through the notch on the clamp. The electrode should remain in the firebox.
6. Carefully lift each burner up and away from the valve openings.

[Manual19_33]

Clean burner tubes using one of these methods:

1. Bend a stiff wire, such as a lightweight coat hanger, into a small hook and run it through each burner tube several times.
2. Use a narrow bottle brush with a flexible handle. Do not use a brass wire brush. Run the brush through each burner tube several times.
3. Wear eye protection and use an air hose to force air into the burner tube and out the burner ports. Check each port to make sure air comes out of each hole.

Then complete the cleaning:

1. Wire-brush the outer surface of the burner to remove food residue and dirt.
2. Clean blocked ports with a stiff wire such as an open paper clip.
3. Check the burner for damage. If large cracks or holes are found, replace the burner.
4. Attach the electrode to the burner.
5. Carefully replace the burners.
6. Attach the burners to the brackets on the firebox.

[Manual19_34]

# 15. Store the grill safely

To store the grill:

1. Clean the cooking grates.
2. Store the grill in a dry location.
3. When the LP tank is connected to the grill, store the grill outdoors in a well-ventilated space and out of reach of children.
4. Cover the grill if stored outdoors.
5. Store the grill indoors only if the LP tank is turned off, disconnected, removed from the grill, and stored outdoors.
6. When removing the grill from storage, follow the burner assembly cleaning instructions before starting the grill.

# 16. Follow food safety guidance

Food safety is an important part of outdoor cooking. To keep food safe from harmful bacteria, follow these four steps:

1. Clean: wash hands, utensils, and surfaces with hot soapy water before and after handling raw meat and poultry.
2. Separate: separate raw meat and poultry from ready-to-eat foods to avoid cross contamination. Use a clean platter and utensils when removing cooked foods.
3. Cook: cook meat and poultry thoroughly to kill bacteria. Use a thermometer to ensure proper internal food temperatures.
4. Chill: refrigerate prepared foods and leftovers promptly.

To tell whether meat is grilled thoroughly:

1. Meat and poultry cooked on a grill often brown very fast on the outside. Use a meat thermometer to make sure food has reached a safe internal temperature, and cut into food to check for visual signs of doneness.
2. Whole poultry should reach 165°F. Juices should run clear and flesh should not be pink.
3. Hamburgers made of ground meat or poultry should reach 160°F and be brown in the middle with no pink juices.
4. Beef, veal, and lamb steaks, roasts, and chops can be cooked to 145°F.
5. All cuts of pork should reach 160°F.
6. Never partially grill meat or poultry and finish cooking later. Cook food completely to destroy harmful bacteria.
7. When reheating takeout foods or fully cooked meats such as hot dogs, grill to 165°F or until steaming hot.

Food must be cooked to the minimum internal temperatures listed in the table.

[Manual19_35]
[Manual19_35 description: The image shows a the title is "USDA* Safe Minimum Internal Temperatures" table. table is divided into two left and right columns, left side columns specific category, right side columns corresponds to safety inside temperature value (unit is Fahrenheit °F). table specific rows content from top to bottom in order are: first row left side is "Fish", right side is "145°F"; second row left side is "Pork", right side is "160°F"; third row left side is "Egg Dishes", right side is "160°F"; fourth row left side is "Steaks and Roasts of Beef, Veal or Lamb", right side is "145°F"; fifth row left side is "Ground Beef, Veal or Lamb", right side is "160°F"; sixth row left side is "Whole Poultry (Turkey, Chicken, Duck, etc. )", right side is "165°F"; seventh rows left side is "Ground or Pieces Poultry (Chicken Breast, etc. )", right side is "165°F".]

# 17. Cook using indirect heat

Poultry and large cuts of meat can cook slowly on the grill using indirect heat. Heat from selected burners circulates gently throughout the grill, cooking meat or poultry without direct flame contact. This method greatly reduces flare-ups when cooking extra-fatty cuts because there is no direct flame to ignite fats and juices that drip during cooking.

[Manual19_36]

One-burner cooking can be used for direct or indirect heat. It is best for smaller meals or foods and consumes less fuel.

Indirect cooking instructions:

1. Always cook with the lid closed.
2. Cooking times may vary with weather conditions.
3. During cold and windy conditions, the temperature setting may need to be increased to ensure sufficient cooking temperature.

[Manual19_37]

Two-burner cooking is useful for indirect cooking on low heat. It produces slow, even heating and is ideal for slow roasting and baking.

section_title: 18. Operate and maintain the grill halogen light
section_path: 18. Operate and maintain the grill halogen light
text:
# 18. Operate and maintain the grill halogen light

Light operation instructions:

1. Make sure the light switch on the control panel is in the OFF position.
2. Connect the light plug to an extension cord, then plug the extension cord into a wall outlet.
3. Turn the light switch to ON.

[Manual19_38]

[Manual19_39]

Keep any electrical supply cord away from heated surfaces. Use the shortest extension cord required. Do not connect two or more extension cords together.

To replace the bulb:

1. Make sure the light switch on the control panel is in the OFF position and the adapter plug is disconnected from the outlet.

[Manual19_40]

2. Release the screw securing the light socket.

[Manual19_41]

3. Take out the socket and remove the lens.

[Manual19_42]

4. Loosen the two screws locking the bulb.

[Manual19_43]

5. Pull out the bulb and replace it with a new bulb.
6. Reverse the instructions to reinstall the socket.

Bulb specification: halogen bulb. The OCR text for wattage and voltage is unclear, so verify the required bulb rating from the original part label before replacement.

Caution: do not touch the bulb with bare fingers. Skin oils can leave a film on the bulb that causes it to burn out quickly.

To clean the lens:

1. Make sure the light switch is OFF and the light plug is disconnected from the power supply.
2. Do not clean the glass lens while it is warm. Allow it to cool before cleaning. Sudden temperature changes may crack the glass lens.
3. Use a damp towel to clean the glass lens surface.
4. Allow the lens to dry before reconnecting the light plug to the power supply and turning the light switch to ON.

Electrical safety for the light:

1. Since 1971, the National Electric Code has required Ground Fault Interrupter devices on all outdoor circuits.
2. If your residence was built before 1971, check with a qualified electrician to determine whether a Ground Fault Interrupter protector exists.
3. Do not use this appliance if the circuit does not have GFI protection.
4. Do not plug this appliance into an indoor circuit.

[Manual19_44]

Additional electrical precautions:

1. To protect against electric shock, do not immerse cords or plugs in water or other liquid.
2. Unplug from the outlet when not in use and before cleaning. Allow to cool before putting on or taking off parts.
3. Do not operate the grill light with a damaged cord or plug, or after malfunction or damage.
4. Do not let the cord hang over the edge of a table or touch hot surfaces.
5. Do not use an outdoor cooking gas appliance for purposes other than intended.
6. When connecting, first connect the plug to the outdoor cooking gas appliance, then plug the appliance into the outlet.
7. Use only a GFI-protected circuit.
8. Never remove the grounding plug or use a two-prong adapter.
9. Use only extension cords with a three-prong grounding plug, rated for the equipment power, and approved for outdoor use with a W-A marking.

section_title: 19. Review parts list and parts diagram
section_path: 19. Review parts list and parts diagram
text:
# 19. Review parts list and parts diagram

Refer to the parts list and parts diagram before assembly. If hardware is missing or parts are damaged, call the listed service number for replacement.

[Manual19_45]

section_title: 20. Assemble the cart, lower back panel, and grill head
section_path: 20. Assemble the cart, lower back panel, and grill head
text:
# 20. Assemble the cart, lower back panel, and grill head

Assembly steps:

1. Attach the two locking casters at the rear of the bottom shelf and the two fixed casters at the front using the supplied wrench.

[Manual19_49]

2. Follow the assembly illustration for step 2.

[Manual19_50]

3. Attach the light adapter to the back panel using four #8-32 × 3/8 inch screws, four 4 mm lock washers, four 4 mm flat washers, and four #8 nuts. Place the lower back panel between the side panels at the rear of the bottom shelf. Secure the lower back panel to the side panels using two 1/4-20 × 1/2 inch screws and two 7 mm lock washers on each side. Secure the lower back panel to the bottom shelf using one 1/4-20 × 1/2 inch screw and one 7 mm lock washer.

[Manual19_51]

Hardware for this step includes four #8-32 × 3/8 inch screws, four 4 mm lock washers, four 4 mm flat washers, five 1/4-20 × 1/2 inch screws, and five 7 mm lock washers.

[Manual19_52]

4. This step requires two people. Carefully lower the grill head onto the cart, aligning the slots at the bottom of the grill head with the posts on the cart side panels. Make sure the regulator hose hangs inside the cart. The grill head must face the open side of the cart.

[Manual19_53]

5. Insert the front brace under the control panel and between the cart side panels. Secure it using two 1/4-20 × 1/2 inch screws and 7 mm lock washers on each side. Make sure the front brace is mounted as shown.

[Manual19_54]

section_title: 21. Install the side shelves, side burner components, wiring, and doors
section_path: 21. Install the side shelves, side burner components, wiring, and doors
text:
# 21. Install the side shelves, side burner components, wiring, and doors

Continue assembly:

1. Remove the two screws and washers from the right side of the firebox front. Insert the flange on the right side shelf into the side shelf brackets on the firebox. Attach the right side shelf front using the two removed screws and washers. Attach the rear of the shelf using one 1/4-20 × 1/2 inch screw, 7 mm lock washer, fiber washer, and 1/4 inch nut.

[Manual19_55]

2. Attach the left side lower fascia to the left side upper fascia using three #10 × 3/8 inch screws, 5 mm lock washers, and 5 mm flat washers. Remove the three screws and washers from the left side of the firebox front. Insert the flange on the left side shelf into the side shelf brackets. Attach the front of the side shelf using the removed screws and washers. Attach the rear of the shelf using one 1/4-20 × 1/2 inch screw, 7 mm lock washer, fiber washer, and 1/4 inch nut.

[Manual19_56]

[Manual19_57]

[Manual19_58]

[Manual19_59]

3. On the back of the grill, place the upper back panel between the side panels and above the lower back panel. Secure it in the lower and upper holes using 1/4-20 × 1/2 inch screws and 7 mm lock washers on each side. Secure the upper back panel to the lower back panel as shown.

[Manual19_60]

4. Remove the two screws and lock washers attached to the side burner valve bracket. Position the side burner valve bracket beneath the side burner shelf fascia so the valve stem passes through the large center hole. Align the valve bracket holes with the fascia holes and secure it using the removed screws and lock washers. Place the side burner bezel over the valve stem on the front of the fascia, making sure OFF is at the top. Attach it using two #8-32 × 3/8 inch screws and 4 mm lock washers. Press the side burner control knob onto the valve stem.

[Manual19_61]

5. Insert the side burner into the left shelf. The stud on the bottom of the burner fits into the rear small hole in the side burner drip pan. Secure the burner to the drip pan with one wing nut. Make sure the burner tube engages the side burner valve.

[Manual19_62]

[Manual19_63]

6. Under the side burner shelf, attach the side burner ignitor wire to the electrode. Place the side burner grate onto the side burner shelf, aligning the grate legs with the holes in the shelf.

[Manual19_64]

[Manual19_65]

7. Connect the adapter wire harness and light wire harness.

[Manual19_66]

8. Inside the cart, insert the rear shield tabs into the slots next to the grease tray opening on the upper back panel. Attach the front shield tabs under the front brace with two #8 × 3/8 inch self-tapping screws.

[Manual19_67]

9. Connect the wires from the main burner electrodes and side burner electrode to the back of the electronic ignition module. There are five electrode connections. Connect the two switch wiring harness wires to the back of the electronic ignition module. The switch terminals are larger than the electrode terminals and should only be installed in the indicated locations. Release the cap and nut from the electronic ignition module. Attach the electronic ignition module and heat shield to the cart left side panel with the nut. Insert an AA battery into the ignition module with the negative end first, then install the cap.

[Manual19_68]

10. Insert the hinge pin on the bottom of each door into the hole in the bottom shelf. Press the upper hinge pin in the front brace, align the hinge hole on top of the door, and release the hinge pin into the door.

[Manual19_69]

11. Place the condiment basket on the inside of the right door. Insert the legs of the condiment basket into the brackets attached to the inside of the door.

section_title: 22. Install heat diffusers, cooking grates, warming rack, LP cylinder, and grease tray
section_path: 22. Install heat diffusers, cooking grates, warming rack, LP cylinder, and grease tray
text:
# 22. Install heat diffusers, cooking grates, warming rack, LP cylinder, and grease tray

Finish assembly:

1. Install heat diffusers by sliding one end of each heat diffuser into the slots at the front of the firebox and resting the opposite end on the pins in the back of the firebox.

[Manual19_71]

2. Place the cooking grates onto the firebox. Insert the two wire ends at the rear of the warming rack into the holes in the back of the firebox. The front wires of the warming rack rest on the sides of the firebox.

[Manual19_72]

3. The LP cylinder is sold separately. Fill and leak-test the cylinder before attaching it to the grill and regulator. Once the cylinder has been filled and leak-tested, place the cylinder into the hole in the bottom shelf. Make sure the cylinder valve faces the front of the grill. Secure the cylinder with the cylinder screw under the bottom shelf. Perform the burner flame check and review all safety instructions before using.

[Manual19_73]

Always keep LP cylinders upright during use, transport, and storage.

[Manual19_74]

The cylinder valve must face the front of the cart once the tank is attached. Failure to install the cylinder correctly may allow the gas hose to be damaged during operation, creating a risk of fire.

[Manual19_75]

4. On the back of the grill, slide the grease tray into the opening in the upper back panel.

Caution: failure to install the grease tray will cause hot grease to drip from the bottom of the grill, creating risk of fire or property damage.

[Manual19_76]

section_title: 1. Manual scope, models, and document retention
section_path: 1. Manual scope, models, and document retention
text:
# 1. Manual scope, models, and document retention

[Manual24_0]

This use and care manual applies to over-the-range microwave models HMV9302, HMV9305, HMV9306, and HMV9307.

Read the entire manual before installing or using the microwave oven. Save these instructions for the local electrical inspector. The installer should leave the installation instructions with the owner, and the owner should keep them for future reference.

The manual covers safety, microwave cooking basics, cookware, parts and accessories, the control panel, cooking programs, sensor cooking, defrosting, food cooking guides, cleaning, light and filter replacement, troubleshooting, and warranty information.

section_title: 2. Precautions to avoid excessive microwave energy exposure
section_path: 2. Precautions to avoid excessive microwave energy exposure
text:
# 2. Precautions to avoid excessive microwave energy exposure

Do not attempt to operate the oven with the door open. Open-door operation can result in harmful exposure to microwave energy. Do not defeat or tamper with the safety interlocks.

Do not place any object between the oven front face and the door. Do not allow soil or cleaner residue to accumulate on sealing surfaces.

Do not operate the oven if it is damaged. It is especially important that the oven door closes properly and that there is no damage to the door, hinges, latches, door seals, or sealing surfaces.

The oven must not be adjusted or repaired by anyone except properly qualified service personnel.

# 3. FCC radio frequency interference statement

Warning: this equipment generates and uses ISM frequency energy. If it is not installed and used in strict accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions, it may cause interference to radio and television reception.

This equipment has been type-tested and found to comply with the limits for ISM equipment under Part 18 of the FCC Rules. These limits are designed to provide reasonable protection against interference in a residential installation.

If the microwave oven causes radio or television interference, which can be determined by turning the equipment off and on, try the following corrective measures:

1. Clean the oven door and sealing surface.
2. Reorient the receiving antenna of the radio or television.
3. Relocate the microwave oven with respect to the receiver.
4. Move the microwave oven away from the receiver.
5. Plug the microwave oven into a different outlet so that the oven and receiver are on different branch circuits.

The manufacturer is not responsible for radio or TV interference caused by unauthorized modification of the microwave oven. The user is responsible for correcting such interference.

section_title: 4. Important safety instructions for using the oven
section_path: 4. Important safety instructions for using the oven
text:
# 4. Important safety instructions for using the oven

Warning: to reduce the risk of burns, electric shock, fire, injury, or exposure to excessive microwave energy, follow these instructions.

Read all instructions before using the oven. Do not allow children to use the oven without close supervision. Read and follow the precautions for avoiding excessive microwave energy exposure.

Do not use corrosive chemicals or vapors, such as sulfide or chloride, in the appliance. This oven is specifically designed to heat, cook, or dry food. It is not designed for industrial or laboratory use.

Do not use or store this appliance outdoors. Do not use it near water, such as near a kitchen sink, in a wet basement, near a swimming pool, or in a similar location.

Do not use the cavity for storage. Do not leave paper products, cooking utensils, or food in the cavity when the oven is not in use.

Clean the ventilating hood frequently. Do not allow grease to accumulate on the hood or filters. Use care when cleaning the vent hood filters because corrosive cleaning agents, such as lye-based oven cleaners, may damage the filters.

Do not tamper with the built-in safety switches on the oven door. The oven has safety switches to make sure the power is off when the door is open.

Always turn the fan on High when cooking foods that might flame up, or whenever flames occur on the cooktop. This oven is suitable for use above gas or electric cooking equipment that is 36 inches wide or less.

Do not use this oven for commercial purposes. It is made for household use only.

When cleaning the door and the surfaces that touch the door, use only mild, non-abrasive soaps or detergents and a sponge or soft cloth.

If the oven is dropped or damaged, have it thoroughly checked by a qualified service technician before using it again.

section_title: 5. Fire, shock, and food-heating safety precautions
section_path: 5. Fire, shock, and food-heating safety precautions
text:
# 5. Fire, shock, and food-heating safety precautions

To avoid fire, do not severely overcook food. Severely overcooked food can start a fire in the oven. Watch the oven carefully when paper, plastic, or other combustible materials are inside.

Do not store combustible items, such as bread or cookies, in the oven. If lightning strikes the power lines, the oven may turn on. Do not use wire twist-ties in the oven. Inspect purchased items and remove any wire twist-ties before placing them in the oven.

If a fire starts inside the oven, keep the oven door closed, turn the oven off, and disconnect the power cord or shut off power at the fuse or circuit breaker panel.

To avoid electric shock, the appliance must be grounded. Connect the oven only to a properly grounded outlet. Do not operate the appliance if the cord or plug is damaged, if it is not working properly, or if it has been damaged or dropped. Do not immerse the electrical cord or plug in water, and keep the cord away from heated surfaces.

To avoid improperly cooking some foods, do not heat baby bottles or baby food, because uneven heating may occur. Do not heat small-necked containers, such as syrup bottles. Do not deep-fat fry or attempt home canning in the microwave oven.

Do not heat whole eggs in the shell, water mixed with oil or fat, sealed containers, or closed glass jars. These items may explode.

Do not cover or block any openings in the oven. Use the oven only for operations described in this manual. Do not run the oven empty. Do not let the cord hang over the edge of a table or counter.

section_title: 6. Protecting the oven floor and preventing liquid boil-over
section_path: 6. Protecting the oven floor and preventing liquid boil-over
text:
# 6. Protecting the oven floor and preventing liquid boil-over

To preserve the oven floor, do not heat the oven floor excessively. Do not allow the gray film on special microwave-cooking packages to touch the oven floor. Place such packages on a microwavable dish.

Do not cook anything directly on the oven floor or turntable. Use a microwavable dish. Keep a browning dish at least 3/16 inch above the oven floor. Follow the browning dish instructions carefully, because incorrect use can damage the oven floor.

Liquids such as water, coffee, or tea can be overheated beyond the boiling point without appearing to boil. Visible bubbling or boiling may not always be present when the container is removed. Very hot liquids may suddenly boil over when the container is disturbed or when a spoon or other utensil is inserted.

To reduce the risk of injury from overheated liquids:

1. Do not overheat the liquid.
2. Stir the liquid before and halfway through heating.
3. Use extreme care when inserting a spoon or other utensil after heating has begun.
4. Do not use straight-sided containers with narrow necks.
5. After heating, allow the container to stand in the microwave oven for a short time before removing it.

# 7. Electrical requirements and grounding instructions

Warning: observe all governing codes and ordinances. A 120 V, 60 Hz, AC-only, 15 or 20 amp fused electrical supply is required. A time-delay fuse is recommended. A separate circuit serving only this appliance is recommended.

Electrical shock hazard: plug into a grounded 3-prong outlet. Do not remove the ground prong. Do not use an adapter. Do not use an extension cord. Failure to follow these instructions can result in death, fire, or electrical shock.

[Manual24_1]

For cord-connected appliances, the microwave oven must be grounded. In the event of an electrical short circuit, grounding reduces the risk of electric shock by providing an escape wire for electric current. The microwave oven has a cord with a grounding wire and grounding plug. The plug must be plugged into an outlet that is properly installed and grounded.

[Manual24_2]

Warning: improper use of grounding can result in electric shock. Consult a qualified electrician or service person if the grounding instructions are not completely understood or if there is doubt whether the microwave oven is properly grounded.

Do not use an extension cord. If the power supply cord is too short, have a qualified electrician or service person install an outlet near the microwave oven.

For a permanently connected appliance, the microwave oven must be connected to a grounded metallic permanent wiring system, or an equipment-grounding conductor must be run with the circuit conductors and connected to the equipment-grounding terminal or lead on the microwave oven.

# 8. Cookware guide for microwave-safe materials

Most heat-resistant, non-metallic cookware is safe for microwave use. To test cookware, place the empty cookware in the microwave oven. Place 1 cup of water in a glass measuring cup beside it. Microwave on 100% power for 1 minute. If the dish becomes warm, do not use it for microwave cooking.

Ovenproof glass treated for high-intensity heat can be used. Examples include utility dishes, bread dishes, pie plates, cake plates, liquid measuring cups, casseroles, and bowls without metallic trim.

China bowls, cups, serving plates, and platters without metallic trim can be used.

Plastic wrap may be used as a cover if the dish is deep enough so the plastic wrap does not touch the food. As food heats, plastic wrap may melt where it touches food. Place plastic wrap loosely over the dish and secure it by pressing it to the sides. Vent by turning back one corner to allow steam to escape.

Use plastic dishes, cups, semi-rigid freezer containers, and plastic bags only for short cooking times. Use them carefully because plastic may soften from the heat of the food.

Microwave-safe paper towels, waxed paper, paper napkins, and paper plates without metallic trim or design can be used. Follow the manufacturer’s label for any paper product used in the microwave oven.

section_title: 9. Cookware and materials that must not be used
section_path: 9. Cookware and materials that must not be used
text:
# 9. Cookware and materials that must not be used

Do not use metal utensils. Metal shields food from microwave energy and causes uneven cooking. Avoid metal skewers, thermometers, or foil trays. Metal utensils can cause arcing, which can damage the microwave oven.

Do not use metal-trimmed or metal-banded dinnerware or casserole dishes.

Do not use Centura tableware or some Corelle closed-handle cups for microwave cooking if the manufacturer warns against it.

Avoid large sheets of aluminum foil because they hinder cooking and may cause arcing. Small pieces of foil may be used to shield poultry legs and wings, but keep all foil at least 1 inch from the oven walls and door.

Do not use wooden bowls, boards, or baskets. Wood can dry out, split, or crack in the microwave oven.

Do not use tightly closed containers. They can explode. Always leave an opening for steam to escape from covered cookware.

Do not use brown paper bags. They absorb heat and could burn.

# 10. General microwave cooking techniques

Browning: meat and poultry with high fat content may brown lightly when cooked for 10 to 15 minutes or longer. Foods cooked for a shorter time can be brushed with a browning agent such as Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, or barbecue sauce.

Covering: a cover traps heat and steam and helps food cook more quickly. Use a lid or microwave-safe plastic wrap with one corner folded back to vent excess steam. Lids on glass casseroles can become hot, so handle them carefully. Waxed paper helps prevent splattering and retain heat. When warming bread items, use waxed paper, napkins, or paper towels.

Spacing: arrange individual foods, such as baked potatoes, cupcakes, and hors d’oeuvres, in a circle at least 1 inch apart so they cook more evenly.

Stirring: stir from the outside toward the center. Food near the outside heats first.

Turning: turn large foods such as roasts and whole poultry during cooking so the top and bottom cook evenly. Turn chicken pieces and chops as well.

Arranging: do not stack food. Arrange food in a single layer. Place thicker portions of meat, poultry, fish, and vegetables toward the outside of the dish because dense foods cook more slowly.

Testing for doneness: microwave foods cook quickly, so check frequently.

Standing time: foods often need to stand for 2 to 15 minutes after cooking, either inside or outside the oven. Cover food during standing time to retain heat. Stop cooking when food is slightly undercooked; it will finish during standing time. The internal temperature of food rises about 10°F during standing time.

Shielding: use small strips of aluminum foil to protect thin or fast-cooking areas, such as poultry legs and wing tips. Keep foil at least 1 inch from oven walls to prevent arcing.

Piercing: pierce shells, skins, or membranes before cooking to prevent bursting. Pierce egg yolks and whites, hot dogs, clams, oysters, and whole vegetables such as potatoes and squash.

section_title: 11. Routine cleaning, removable parts, and special care
section_path: 11. Routine cleaning, removable parts, and special care
text:
# 11. Routine cleaning, removable parts, and special care

Wipe the inside and outside of the oven with a soft cloth and mild detergent solution, then rinse and wipe dry. Clean weekly or more often if needed. Never use cleaning powders or rough pads. Excessive oil splatter on the inside top is difficult to remove if left for several days. Wipe splatters with a wet paper towel, especially after cooking chicken or bacon.

The turntable and turntable roller rest are removable. Wash them by hand in warm, not hot, water with mild detergent and a soft cloth. Rinse and dry well. Never use cleaning powders, steel wool, or rough pads.

The turntable may be cleaned in the sink. Be careful not to chip or scratch the edges because this may cause it to break during use. Clean the turntable roller rest regularly.

For best performance and safety, keep the inner door panel and oven front frame free of food or grease buildup. Wipe often with mild detergent, then rinse and wipe dry. Never use cleaning powders or rough pads.

After cleaning the control panel, touch Stop/Clear to clear any entries that might have been entered accidentally.

text:
# 14. Vent, turntable, child lock, and cooktop light controls

The Vent pad moves steam and other vapors from the cooking surface. From Off, the first touch turns the vent to High, the second touch changes it to Low, and the third touch turns it off.

If the area around the microwave becomes too hot, the vent hood fan automatically turns on at the Low setting. It may stay on for up to one hour. During this time, the vent fan cannot be turned off manually.

For best cooking results, leave the turntable on. It can be turned off for large dishes by pressing Turntable On/Off. The Turntable On/Off feature does not operate during Defrost or Sensor cooking modes. The turntable can become hot during and after cooking. Do not run the oven empty.

Child Lock locks the control panel so it cannot be operated. To set it, touch Stop/Clear once, then touch and hold 0 for more than four seconds. Locked appears in the display and two beeps sound. To cancel Child Lock, touch and hold 0 for more than four seconds. Locked disappears and two beeps sound.

Touch the Light pad once for bright light, again for low light, and a third time to turn the light off.

# 15. Light Timer operation

The Light Timer can turn the low light on and off automatically at set times. The light turns on at the low setting at the same time every day and turns off at the programmed time until reset.

section_title: 18. Sensor cooking instructions and sensor cooking guide
section_path: 18. Sensor cooking instructions and sensor cooking guide
text:
# 18. Sensor cooking instructions and sensor cooking guide

Sensor Cook lets the oven cook many foods without requiring manual cooking times or power levels. The oven automatically determines the required cooking time. During the initial sensing period, the display indicates Sensing. When the internal sensor detects humidity from the food, it tells the oven how much longer to heat, and the display shows the remaining heating time.

For best sensor cooking results:

1. Food should be at normal storage temperature.
2. The glass turntable and the outside of the container should be dry.
3. Foods should be covered loosely with microwavable plastic wrap, waxed paper, or a lid.
4. Do not open the door or touch Stop/Clear during sensing time. When sensing time ends, the oven beeps twice and the remaining cook time appears. At that point, you can open the door to stir, turn, or rearrange the food.

Use microwavable containers and cover them with lids or vented plastic wrap. Never use tight-sealing plastic covers, because they prevent steam from escaping and can overcook food. Match the amount of food to the container size, and fill containers at least half full when possible. Make sure the outside of the container and the inside of the oven are dry.

To adjust sensor cook time, use More or Less after selecting the sensor function. Cooking time can be increased or decreased by 10 seconds while Sensor is displayed.

# 23. Time Defrost, Quick Defrost, and two-position metal rack

section_title: 24. Guidelines for best microwave cooking results
section_path: 24. Guidelines for best microwave cooking results
text:
# 24. Guidelines for best microwave cooking results

For best results, consider food temperature, size, moisture, arrangement, stirring, turning, shielding, standing time, and wrapping.

Foods taken from the freezer or refrigerator take longer to cook than foods at room temperature. Small pieces cook faster than large pieces. Pieces of similar size and shape cook more evenly. For even cooking, reduce power when cooking large pieces.

Very moist foods cook more evenly because microwave energy is attracted to water molecules.

Stir casseroles and vegetables from the outside toward the center to distribute heat evenly and speed cooking. Occasional stirring is usually sufficient.

Turn foods such as pork chops, whole potatoes, roasts, and whole cauliflower halfway through cooking to expose all sides evenly.

Place delicate areas, such as asparagus tips, toward the center of the dish. Arrange unevenly shaped foods, such as chicken pieces or salmon steaks, with thicker parts toward the outside.

Shield thin or fast-cooking parts, such as poultry wing tips and leg ends, with small pieces of aluminum foil. Keep foil at least 1 inch from oven walls and from other pieces of foil.

After removing food from the microwave, cover it with foil or a casserole lid and let it stand so the center finishes cooking without overcooking the outer edges. Standing time depends on the food’s density and surface area.

Wrap sandwiches and other foods containing pre-baked bread in waxed paper or paper towel before microwaving to prevent drying.

section_title: 25. Fish, shellfish, appetizers, sauces, and soups
section_path: 25. Fish, shellfish, appetizers, sauces, and soups
text:
# 25. Fish, shellfish, appetizers, sauces, and soups

For fish and shellfish, defrost completely before cooking. Arrange unevenly shaped pieces with thicker parts toward the outside of the dish. Arrange shellfish in a single layer for even cooking.

Poached fish needs a microwavable lid or vented plastic wrap. Baked fish, coated fish, or fish in sauce should be covered lightly with waxed paper to keep coating crisp and prevent sauce from becoming watery.

Use the shortest cooking time first. Fish is done when it turns opaque and the thickest part begins to flake. Shellfish is done when the shell changes from pink to red and the flesh is opaque and firm.

The fish and shellfish cooking table provides specific power levels and cooking times.

For appetizers, crisp crackers such as melba toast, shredded wheat, and crisp rye crackers work best. Add spreads just before serving. Place a paper towel under crackers to absorb moisture. Arrange individual appetizers in a circle for even cooking.

For sauces, use a microwavable casserole or glass measuring cup at least 2 or 3 times the volume of the sauce. Sauces made with cornstarch thicken more quickly than sauces made with flour. Cook sauces made with cornstarch or flour uncovered so they can be stirred 2 or 3 times for smooth consistency.

For soups, use a microwavable dish that holds double the volume of the recipe to prevent boil-over, especially for soups with cream or milk. Generally cover soups with vented plastic wrap or a microwavable lid. Reduce liquid, salt, and strong seasonings when converting a conventional soup recipe for microwave cooking.

Appetizers with a crisp coating or puff pastry are not recommended for microwave cooking; they are better cooked in a conventional oven. Breaded products can be warmed in the microwave but will not become crisp.

# 26. Meat cooking guidance

Defrost meat completely before cooking. Trim excess fat to reduce splattering. Place meat fat side down on a microwavable rack in a microwavable dish. Use an oven cooking bag for less tender cuts.

Arrange meat so thicker portions are toward the outside of the dish. Cover meat with waxed paper to prevent splattering.

As meat cooks, drain juices as they accumulate to reduce splattering and prevent the bottom from overcooking. Shield thin or bony portions with strips of foil to prevent overcooking.

Keep foil at least 1 inch from oven walls, and do not cover more than one-third of the meat with foil at any one time.

Let meat stand covered with foil for 10 to 15 minutes after removing it from the oven. The internal temperature may rise 5°F to 10°F during standing time.

The meat cooking table provides detailed directions, power levels, and cooking time settings for most cuts of meat.

# 27. Poultry cooking guidance

Defrost poultry completely before cooking. Arrange poultry pieces with thicker pieces toward the outside edge of the baking dish. When cooking legs, arrange them like spokes of a wheel.

Cover the baking dish with waxed paper to reduce splattering. Use a browning agent, such as Worcestershire sauce, or cook with a sauce to give poultry a browned appearance.

Watch poultry as it cooks. Drain and discard juices as they accumulate. Shield thin or bony pieces with small strips of aluminum foil to prevent overcooking. Keep foil at least 1 inch from the oven walls and from other foil pieces.

Poultry is done when it is no longer pink and the juices run clear. When done, the temperature in thigh meat should be 180°F to 185°F.

Let poultry stand covered with foil for 10 minutes after cooking.

The poultry cooking table provides detailed directions, power levels, and cooking time settings for most cuts and types of poultry.

# 28. Pasta and rice cooking guidance

Microwave cooking and conventional cooking of pasta, rice, and cereal require about the same amount of time, but the microwave is more convenient because food can be cooked and served in the same dish.

There is no stirring needed during cooking, and leftover pasta tastes like freshly cooked pasta when reheated in the microwave oven.

If rice or pasta will be used in a casserole, undercook it so it remains firm. Allow standing time for rice, but not for pasta.

section_title: 29. Care and cleaning of the oven and metal rack
section_path: 29. Care and cleaning of the oven and metal rack
text:
# 29. Care and cleaning of the oven and metal rack

For best performance and safety, keep the oven clean inside and outside. Take special care to keep the inner door panel and oven front frame free of food and grease buildup.

Never use rough powder or pads. Wipe the microwave oven inside and outside, including the hood bottom cover, with a soft cloth and warm, not hot, mild detergent solution. Rinse and wipe dry.

Use a chrome cleaner and polish on chrome, metal, and aluminum surfaces. Wipe spatters immediately with a wet paper towel, especially after cooking chicken or bacon. Clean the oven weekly or more often if needed.

Wash the metal rack with mild soap and a soft or nylon scrub brush. Dry completely. Do not use abrasive scrubbers or cleaners on the rack.

# 30. Cleaning the grease filter

The grease filter should be removed and cleaned often, at least once a month.

1. To remove the grease filter, slide it to the side. Pull the filter downward and push it to the other side. The filter will drop out.

[Manual24_47]

2. Wash the filter in a dishwasher or soak it in hot water with mild detergent. Rinse well and shake dry. Do not use ammonia. If washed in a dishwasher, the aluminum filter may darken.

[Manual24_48]

3. To reinstall the filter, slide it into the side slot, then push it up and toward the oven center to lock it.

[Manual24_49]

Caution: to avoid personal injury or property damage, do not operate the oven hood without the filter in place.

# 31. Replacing the charcoal filter

If the oven is vented indoors, replace the charcoal filter every 6 to 12 months, or more often if necessary. The charcoal filter cannot be cleaned.

1. Unplug the oven or turn off power at the main power supply.
2. Remove the two vent grille mounting screws.

[Manual24_50]

3. Tip the grille forward, then lift it out.
4. Remove the old filter.

[Manual24_51]

5. Slide a new charcoal filter into place. The filter should rest at the angle shown.

[Manual24_52]

6. Slide the bottom of the grille into place. Push the top until it snaps into place. Replace the mounting screws. Turn power back on at the main power supply and set the clock.

section_title: 32. Replacing the cooktop light and oven light
section_path: 32. Replacing the cooktop light and oven light
text:
# 32. Replacing the cooktop light and oven light

To replace the cooktop or night light:

1. Unplug the oven or turn off power at the main power supply.

[Manual24_53]

2. Remove the bulb cover and mounting screws.
3. Replace the bulb or bulbs with 30 or 40 watt appliance bulbs.
4. Replace the bulb cover and mounting screws.
5. Turn power back on at the main power supply or plug in the oven.

Caution: to avoid personal injury or property damage, wear gloves when replacing the light bulb.

To replace the oven light:

1. Unplug the oven or turn off power at the main power supply.
2. Remove the vent cover mounting screws.
3. Tip the cover forward, then lift it out.

[Manual24_54]

4. Remove the bulb holder.

[Manual24_55]

5. Lift up the bulb holder.

[Manual24_56]

6. Replace the bulb with a 30 or 40 watt appliance bulb.
7. Replace the bulb holder.
8. Slide the bottom of the vent cover into place. Push the top until it snaps into place. Replace the mounting screws, then turn power back on or plug in the oven.

section_title: 1. Product Overview and Safety Before Use
section_path: 1. Product Overview and Safety Before Use
text:
# 1. Product Overview and Safety Before Use

This robot vacuum is designed for indoor floor cleaning and uses a battery-powered robot body with a Home Base charging dock.

[Manual32_0]

Before using the robot vacuum, read all safety and operating instructions and keep them for future reference. Follow all warnings on the robot vacuum, battery, Home Base, and in the owner's guide.

Important safety requirements:

- Do not expose the electronics, battery, or integrated dock charger. There are no user-serviceable parts inside. Refer servicing to qualified service personnel.
- Make sure the voltage rating of the enclosed power supply matches your standard outlet voltage.
- Use the robot vacuum only in dry indoor environments.
- Do not spray or pour liquids on the robot vacuum.
- Do not operate the robot vacuum in areas with exposed electrical outlets in the floor.
- The robot vacuum moves on its own. Take care when walking in the area where it is operating to avoid stepping on it.
- Do not place anything on top of the robot vacuum.
- Do not use any power supply cord other than the region-approved cord supplied with the robot vacuum.

Before each cleaning run, pick up objects such as clothing, loose papers, pull cords for blinds or curtains, power cords, and fragile items. If the robot vacuum passes over a power cord and drags it, objects may be pulled off a table or shelf.

If the room contains a balcony, use a physical barrier to prevent access to the balcony and ensure safe operation.

The robot vacuum is not intended for use by persons, including children, with reduced physical, sensory, or mental capabilities, or lack of experience and knowledge, unless they have been supervised or instructed by a person responsible for their safety. Children should be supervised to ensure that they do not play with the robot vacuum. Cleaning and maintenance must not be performed by children without supervision.

# 2. Use Restrictions

Use the robot vacuum only for indoor household floor cleaning.

Restrictions:

- The robot vacuum is not a toy. Do not sit or stand on it.
- Small children and pets should be supervised when the robot vacuum is operating.
- Store and operate the robot vacuum only in room-temperature environments.
- Clean the iAdapt localization camera with a cloth dampened with water only.
- Do not use the robot vacuum to pick up anything that is burning or smoking.
- Do not use the robot vacuum to pick up spills of bleach, paint, chemicals, or anything wet.

# 3. Battery and Charging Safety

Charge the robot vacuum using a standard outlet only. The robot vacuum must not be used with any type of power converter. Use of other power converters will immediately void the warranty.

Battery and charging requirements:

- Use only rechargeable battery packs with the correct specification.
- Do not use the robot vacuum with a damaged cord or plug.
- Charge indoors only.
- Always disconnect the robot vacuum from the Home Base before cleaning or maintaining it.
- Never handle the robot vacuum or charger with wet hands.
- Always charge the battery before long-term storage or transportation.
- Remove the battery from the robot vacuum before long-term storage or transportation.
- Before every use, check the battery pack for any sign of damage or leakage.
- Do not charge damaged or leaking battery packs.
- The battery pack must be removed before disposal.
- Do not heat the battery pack or place it near any heat source.
- Do not incinerate the battery pack.
- Do not short-circuit the battery pack.
- Do not immerse the battery pack in any liquid.

Used battery packs should be placed in a sealed plastic bag and disposed of safely according to local environmental regulations. Contact your local waste management authority for battery recycling and disposal regulations.

Do not dispose of electrical appliances as unsorted municipal waste. Use separate collection facilities. If electrical appliances are disposed of in landfills or dumps, hazardous substances can leak into groundwater and enter the food chain, damaging health and well-being.

section_title: 5. Positioning the Home Base, Activating the Robot, and Connecting Wi-Fi
section_path: 5. Positioning the Home Base, Activating the Robot, and Connecting Wi-Fi
text:
# 5. Positioning the Home Base, Activating the Robot, and Connecting Wi-Fi

Place the Home Base in an open, uncluttered area with these clearances:

- At least 1.5 ft on each side.
- At least 4 ft in front.
- At least 4 ft away from stairs.
- At least 8 ft from virtual wall barriers.

Always keep the Home Base plugged in. Place it in an area with consistent wireless coverage so the robot vacuum can receive information through the app.

To activate the robot vacuum:

1. Turn the robot vacuum over.
2. Remove the yellow bin insert and battery pull tab.
3. Place the robot vacuum on the Home Base to activate the battery.

The robot vacuum has a partial battery charge when shipped, so it is ready to begin cleaning.

To connect to Wi-Fi and the app:

1. Download the app.
2. Watch the overview video for setup and use instructions.
3. Connect the robot vacuum to Wi-Fi.
4. Set an automatic cleaning schedule, up to 7 times per week.
5. Customize cleaning preferences.
6. Enable automatic software updates.
7. Use the app for tips, tricks, support, and answers to common questions.

section_title: 6. Starting, Pausing, Resuming, and Ending a Cleaning Cycle
section_path: 6. Starting, Pausing, Resuming, and Ending a Cleaning Cycle
text:
# 6. Starting, Pausing, Resuming, and Ending a Cleaning Cycle

Before cleaning, remove excess clutter from floors, such as clothing and toys. Use the robot vacuum frequently to maintain well-conditioned floors.

To wake and start the robot vacuum manually:

1. Press CLEAN once. The robot vacuum beeps and the CLEAN button illuminates.
2. Press CLEAN again to start a cleaning cycle.

You can also start a cleaning cycle by pressing CLEAN on the app home screen.

During cleaning:

- To pause the robot vacuum, press CLEAN.
- To resume the cleaning cycle, press CLEAN again.
- To end the cleaning cycle and put the robot vacuum in standby mode, press and hold CLEAN until the indicators turn off.
- To send the robot vacuum back to its Home Base during a cleaning cycle, press CLEAN and then DOCK, or press CLEAN on the app main screen. This ends the cleaning cycle.
- You can check the app for the current status of the robot vacuum.

If the battery gets low before the cleaning cycle is finished, the robot vacuum returns to recharge. It will not play a tone when it docks, and the CLEAN button will pulse with the battery indicator. After the battery has recharged, the robot vacuum automatically returns to where it left off and completes the cleaning cycle.

If the robot vacuum returns to recharge after completing a cleaning cycle, it will play a series of tones to indicate successful completion.

section_title: 7. Spot Cleaning and Full Bin Behavior
section_path: 7. Spot Cleaning and Full Bin Behavior
text:
# 7. Spot Cleaning and Full Bin Behavior

If the robot vacuum encounters an area with a high concentration of debris, it moves in a forward and backward motion to clean the area more thoroughly. When this happens, the debris-detection indicator illuminates.

To use Spot Cleaning:

1. Place the robot vacuum on top of the localized debris.
2. Press SPOT on the robot.
3. The robot vacuum intensely cleans the area by spiraling outward about 3 ft in diameter, then spiraling inward to where it started.

When the robot vacuum senses that its dust bin is full, it is programmed to complete the current cleaning cycle by default. You can adjust this setting under Cleaning Preferences in the app.

The robot vacuum will not leave for a cleaning cycle if its bin is full. In this case, remove and empty the bin, then reinsert it before starting or resuming a cleaning cycle.

After each use, empty the bin and clean the filter.

Always store the robot vacuum on the Home Base so it is charged and ready to clean. If storing it away from the Home Base, remove the battery first, then store the robot vacuum and battery in a cool, dry place.

section_title: 8. Using the Dual Mode Virtual Wall Barrier
section_path: 8. Using the Dual Mode Virtual Wall Barrier
text:
# 8. Using the Dual Mode Virtual Wall Barrier

The Dual Mode Virtual Wall Barrier keeps the robot vacuum in the areas you want cleaned and out of areas you want to protect. Between cleaning cycles, you can leave the device operating in its position on the floor. Set the device to one of two modes to fit your home cleaning needs.

[Manual32_4]

Under normal use, batteries in the virtual wall device will last 8 to 10 months. If you are not planning to use the virtual wall device for an extended period and want to store it, switch it to the Off position in the middle.

**Halo Mode:** When the switch is in the down position, the device creates a protective zone that the robot vacuum will not enter. This prevents the robot vacuum from bumping into items you want to protect, such as a dog bowl or vase, or crossing into undesired areas, such as a corner or under a desk. The halo is invisible and reaches approximately 24 inches from the center of the device.

[Manual32_5]

**Virtual Wall Mode:** When the switch is in the up position, the device functions as a virtual wall. It can block openings up to 10 ft. It creates an invisible cone-shaped barrier that only the robot vacuum can detect. The barrier gets wider as it gets farther from the device.

[Manual32_6]

# 9. Routine Care Overview

To keep the robot vacuum running at peak performance, perform routine care procedures regularly. If the robot vacuum picks up less debris from your floor, empty the bin, clean the filter, and clean the extractors.

[Manual32_7]
