# 10. Emptying the Bin and Cleaning the Filter

To empty the bin:

1. Press the bin release button to remove the bin.

[Manual32_8]

2. Open the bin door and empty the bin.

[Manual32_9]

If the full bin indicator comes on during a cleaning job, you can pause the cleaning job, empty the bin, and then continue cleaning. If the full bin indicator is illuminated but the bin does not appear to be full, clean the full bin sensors.

To clean the filter:

1. Remove the filter by grasping the yellow tab.

[Manual32_10]

2. Shake off debris by tapping the filter against your trash container.

[Manual32_11]

Important: The filter door will not close unless a filter is reinserted. Insert the filter with the yellow tab facing up.

section_title: 11. Cleaning the Full Bin Sensors, Caster Wheel, Side Brush, and Contacts
section_path: 11. Cleaning the Full Bin Sensors, Caster Wheel, Side Brush, and Contacts
text:
# 11. Cleaning the Full Bin Sensors, Caster Wheel, Side Brush, and Contacts

To clean the full bin sensors:

1. Remove and empty the bin.

[Manual32_12]

2. Wipe the sensors with a clean, dry cloth.

[Manual32_13]

3. Wipe the inner and outer sensor ports on the bin with a clean, dry cloth.

[Manual32_14]

To clean the front caster wheel:

1. Pull firmly on the front wheel to remove it.

[Manual32_15]

2. Remove any debris from inside the wheel cavity.
3. Spin the wheel by hand. If rotation is restricted, remove the wheel from its housing and push firmly to remove the axle. Clear any debris or hair wrapped around it.
4. Reinstall all parts when finished. Make sure the wheel clicks back into place.

To clean the side brush:

1. Use a coin or small screwdriver to remove the screw.

[Manual32_16]

2. Remove the brush.
3. Clean the brush and the brush post.
4. Reinstall the brush.

To clean the sensors and charging contacts:

1. Wipe the sensor with a clean, dry cloth. Do not spray cleaning solution directly onto the sensors or sensor openings.

[Manual32_17]

2. Wipe the charging contacts on the robot vacuum and the Home Base with a clean, dry cloth.

[Manual32_18]

# 12. Cleaning the Extractors

To clean the extractors:

1. Pinch the yellow extractor frame release tabs, lift up the extractor frame, and remove any obstructions.

[Manual32_19]

2. Remove the extractors and remove the yellow extractor caps. Remove any hair or debris collected underneath the caps and around the metal axles. Reinstall the extractor caps.

[Manual32_20]

3. Remove hair and debris from the square and hexagonal plastic pegs on the other side of the extractors.

[Manual32_21]

4. Clear the vacuum path.

[Manual32_22]

5. Reinstall the extractors. Match the color and shape of the extractor pegs with the color and shape of the extractor icons on the cleaning head module.

# 13. Troubleshooting and Rebooting

The robot vacuum indicates a problem with a two-tone distress sound followed by a spoken message. The troubleshooting indicator also blinks. More detailed support and videos are available through the app and online.

For some errors, rebooting the robot vacuum may resolve the problem.

To reboot the robot vacuum:

1. Press and hold CLEAN for 10 seconds until all indicators illuminate.
2. Release CLEAN.
3. When you release the CLEAN button, you will hear an audible tone confirming a successful reboot.

If you use the scheduling feature, open the app after rebooting to confirm that the schedule remains intact.

section_title: 14. Reduced Power Standby Mode and Lithium Ion Battery Shipping
section_path: 14. Reduced Power Standby Mode and Lithium Ion Battery Shipping
text:
# 14. Reduced Power Standby Mode and Lithium Ion Battery Shipping

The robot vacuum consumes a small amount of power whenever it is ready for the next cleaning job and maintaining Wi-Fi connectivity. You can place the robot vacuum in a further-reduced power state when it is not in use. Refer to the app for instructions and details about reduced power standby mode.

For best results, use only the lithium ion battery that comes with the robot vacuum. The robot vacuum may operate with older-model batteries, but performance will be limited.

Lithium ion batteries and products containing lithium ion batteries are subject to strict transportation regulations. If you need to ship this product with the battery included for service, travel, or any other reason, follow these shipping instructions:

1. Remove the lithium ion battery from the product.
2. Place a piece of tape over the battery's metal charging contacts.
3. Reinstall the battery, with the tape on it, in the product.
4. Secure the battery door.
5. Package the product in its original packaging, or in packaging that prevents movement during transportation.
6. Ship by ground transportation only. Do not ship by air.

# 16. Break-in and learning to ride

**BREAK-IN.**
There is never a more Important: period in the life of your machine than the Break-In period. For the first 10 hours, approximately 200 km (125 mi)$, do not put an excessive load on the engine. Avoid prolonged full throttle operation. Also avoid lugging the engine, such as laborious operation inwet snow. If any abnormal condition is noticed, suchas excessive vibration or noise, consult a dealer.

**RIDING YOUR SNOWMOBILE.**

**GETTING TO KNOW YOUR SNOWMOBILE.**
A snowmobile is a rider active vehicle, and your riding position and your balance are the two basic factors of maneuvering your snowmobile. Riding your snowmobilerequires skills acquired through practice over a period of time. Take the time to learn the basic techniques well before attempting more difficult maneuvers. Riding your new snowmobile can be a very enjoyable activity, providing you with hours of pleasure. But it is essential to familiarize yourself with the operation of the snowmobile to achieve the skill necessary to enjoy riding safely. Before you begin to ride, be sureyou have read this Owner's Manual completely and understand the operation of the controls. Pay particular attention to the safety information on page 3-1 3-3 Please read all Warning: and Caution: labels on your snowmobile. Also read the Snowmobile r's Safety Handbook originally supplied with your machine.

**LEARNING TO RIDE YOUR SNOWMOBILE.**
Before you ride, always perform the Pre-operation checks listed on page 8-1 8-3 The short time spent checking the condition of the machine will be rewarded with added safety and a more reliable snowmobile. Always wear the proper clothing for both warmth and to help protect you from injury if an accident occurs. Become familiar with this snowmobile at slow speeds even if you are an experienced operator. Do not attempt to operate at maximum performance until you are totally familiar with the machine's handling and performance characteristics. The beginning operator should select a large, flat area to become familiar with the snowmobile. Make sure that this areais freeof obstacles and other traffic. You should practice control of the throttle and brake, and master turning techniques in this area before trying more difficult terrain.
Set the parking brake and follow the instructions on page 7-1 7-2 to start the engine. Once it has warmed up, you are ready to begin riding your snowmobile.

**TO START OUT AND ACCELERATE.**
1. With the engine idling, release theparking brake
2. Apply the throttle slowly and smoothly. The centrifugal clutch will engage and you will start to accelerate.

Warning: The operator should always keep both hands on the handlebars. Never put your feet outside the running boards. Avoid higher speeds until you have become thoroughly familiar with your snowmobile and all of its controls.

# 17. Braking and turning

**BRAKING.**
When slowing down or stopping, release the throttle and apply the brake gently-not suddenly.

Warning: Many surfaces such as ice and hard-packed snow require muchlonger stopping distances. Bealert, plan ahead and begin decelerating early. Improper use of the brake can cause the drive track to lose traction, reducing control and increasing the possibility of an accident.

**TURNING.**
For most snow surfaces, "body English" is the key to turning. As you approach a curve, slowdown and begin to turn the handlebars in the desired direction. As you do so, put your weight on the running board to the inside of the turn and lean your upperbody into the turn. This procedure should be practiced at slow speed many times in a large flat area with no obstacles. Once you have learned this technique, you should be able to perform it at higher speeds or in tighter curves. Lean more as the turn gets sharper or is made at higher speeds
Improper riding procedures such as abrupt throttle changes excessive braking, incorrect body movements, ortoomuch speed for the sharpness of the turn may cause the snowmobile to tip. If your snowmobile begins to tip while turning, lean more into the turn to regain balance. If necessary, gradually let off on the throttle and/orsteer to the outside of theturn.
[Manual34_127]

**Remember:.**
Avoid higher speeds until you are thoroughly familiar with the operation of your snowmobile

text:
# 18. Riding uphill, downhill, and across slopes

**RIDING UPHILL.**
You should practice first on gentle slopes. Try more difficult climbs only after you have developed your skill. Asyou approacha hill, accelerate before you start the climb, and then reduce the throttle opening to prevent track slippage. It is also Important: tokeep your weight on the uphill side at alltimes. On climbs straight upthehill this canbeaccomplished byleaning forward and, on steeper inclines, standin gon the running boards and leaning forward over the handlebars.(AIsosee"CROSSING A SLOPE.") Slowdown as your each the crest of the hill, andbe prepared to react to obstacles, sharp drops, or other people or vehicles which may be on the other side. If you are unable to continue up a hill, do not spin the track. Stop the engine and set the parking brake. Then pull the rear of the snowmobile around to point the machine back down the hill. Do not get on the downhill side of the machine. When the snowmobile is pointed downhill, restart the engine, release the parking brake, anddescend the hill.

Warning: Side hills and steep slopes are not recommended for a beginner or novice snowmobiler.

**RIDING DOWNHILL.**
When riding downhill, keep speed to a minimum. It is Important: to apply just enough throttle to keep the clutch engaged while descending the hill. This will allow you to use engine compression to help slow the machine, and to keep the snowmobile from rolling freely down the hill. Also apply the brake frequently, withlight pressure.
[Manual34_128]

Warning: Use extra Caution: when applying the brake during descent. Excessive braking will cause the track to lock and will cause a loss of control.

**CROSSING A SLOPE (SIDE HILL).**

Warning: Side hills are not recommended for a beginner or novice snowmobiler. Crossing thefaceofa slope(side hill)requires you to properly position your weight to maintain proper balance. As you travel across the slope, lean your body to position your weight towards the uphill side. A recommended riding position is to kneel with the knee of the downhill leg on the seat and the foot of the uphill leg on the running board. This position will make it easier for you to shift your body weight asneeded. Snowand ice are slippery, so be prepared for the possibility that your snowmobile could begin to slip sideways on theslope. If this happens, steerin the direction of theslide if there areno obstacles in your path. As you regain proper balance, gradually steer again in the direction you wish to travel. If your snowmobile starts to tip, steer down the hill toregain balance.
[Manual34_129]

Warning: If you are unable to maintain correct balance, andyour snowmobile is going to tip over, dismount your snowmobile immediately on the uphill side.
Operating on ice or icy surfaces can be very dangerous Traction for turning, stopping or starting is much less than thatonsnow.

section_path: 19. Riding on ice, hard-packed snow, and other surfaces
text:
# 19. Riding on ice, hard-packed snow, and other surfaces

Warning: When you have to operate on ice or icy surfaces, drive slowly and cautiously. Avoid rapid acceleration, turn ing or braking. Steering is minimal and uncontrolled spins area never-present danger.

**Hard-packed snow.**
It can be more difficult to negotiate on hard-packed snow as both skis and track do not have as much traction. Avoid rapid acceleration, turning or braking.

**OPERATION ON SURFACES OTHER THAN SNOW ORICE.**
Operation of your snowmobile on surfaces other than ice or snow should be avoided. Operation under such cond it ions will damage or result in rapid wear of ski runners, drivetrack, slide runners and drive sprockets. Operation of the machine under the following conditions should be avoided at all costs:
1. Dirt
2. Sand
3. Rocks
4. Grass
5. Bare pavement Other conditions that should be avoided for the sake of drive track and slide runner life are:
1. Glare ice surfaces
2. Snow mixed with a lot of dirt and s and All the above conditions have one thing in common in regard to drive track and slide runners; little or no lubricating ability. Drive track and all slide rail systems require lubrication(snowor water)between the plastic runners and the metal track inserts. In the absence of lubrication, the plastic runners will rapidly wear and in severe cases, literally melt away, and the drive track will be subjected to damageand/orfailure. Also, traction aids such as studs, cleats etc., maycause further track damage and/orfailure.
Drive track damage and/or failure could result in loss of braking ability and machine control, which could cause an accident. Always check thedrive track for damage or misadjustment before operating the machine. Do not operate the machine if you find damage to the drive track.

Caution: Be sure to ride on the fresh snow frequently to avoid rapid wear and damage of the drive track and slide runners when operating under ice or hard-packed snow conditions.

# 20. Driving procedures, stopping, and transporting

**TRANSPORTING.**
When transporting your machine on a trailer or in a truck. observe the following recommendations to help protect your machine from damage: Makesure the fuel level in the fuel tank is lower than the carburetors. Otherwise, the vibration and bumps from the road surface could make it possible for fuel to flow through the carburetor into the crankcase. Thiscan resultin"hydrostatic lock,"a condition where the engine cannot rotate because of fuel accumulated in the engine. Severe engine damage can result from hydrostatic lock. When possible, the fuel tank should be empty during transportation, especially if the trip will be 30 minutes or longer. If transporting the machine in an open trailer or truck put a tight fitting cover on the machine. A cover spec if icall y designed for your snowmobile is best. Thiswill help keep foreign objects outof the cooling vents in the shroud, and also help protect the machine against damage from debris on the road. If transporting the machine in an open trailer or truck in areas where road salt is used, coat metal suspension surface slightly with oil or other protectant. This will help protect against corrosion. Be sure to clean the machine when you get to your destination to remove any corrosive salts

# 21. Tool kit and spark plug inspection

**TOOL KIT.**
Theowner's toolkit has the tools which are sufficient for most periodic maintenance and minor repair. A torque wrenchis also necessary to properly tighten nuts andbolts (1) Tool kit

Note: If you do not have a torque wrench available during a service operation requiring one, take your machine to a dealer to check the torque settings and adjust them if necessary. BR250T BCS340E ET410TR VK540E
[Manual34_137]

**SPARK PLUG INSPECTION.**
The spark plug is an Important: engine component and is easy to inspect. The condition of the spark plug can indicate something of the condition of the engine. Check the coloration on the white porcelain insulator around the center electrode. The ideal coloration at this point is a medium to a light tan color for a machine that is being ridden normally. If a spark plug shows a distinctly different color, there could be something wrong with the engine. For example, a very white center electrode porcelain color could indicate an in take track air leak or carburetion problem for that cylinder. Do not attempt to diagnose such problems yourself. Instead, take the machine to your dealer. You should periodically remove and inspec t the spark plug because heat and deposits will cause any spark plug to slowly breakdown and erode. Consult your dealer before changing to a different type of spark plug.
Spark plugs are produced in several different thread lengths. The thread length (reach) is the distance from the spark plug gaskets eat to the end of the threaded portion. If the reach is too long, overheating and engine damage mayresult. If the reach is too short, spark plug fouling and poor performance mayresult. Also, if too short, carbonwill form on the exposed threads resulting in combustion chamber hot spots and thread damage. Always use a spark plug with the proper reach.

text:
# 23. High-altitude adjustment and fan belt check

**High altitude adjustments.**
Operating at high altitude reduces the performance of a gasoline engine, about 3% forevery 305 m (1000ft)of elevation. This is because there is less air as altitude increases. Less air means less oxygen available for combustion. Your snowmobile can be adjusted to overcome most of the problems found in high altitude riding. Carburetor adjustments are the most Important:. Less air at high altitude makes the fuel/air ratio too rich, which can cause poor performance. Common problems are hard starting, bogging, and plug fouling. Follow the Main Jet Setting chart which is available at an authorized dealer carefully. Proper carburetion adjustments will correct the fuel/air ratio. Remember: less air at higher altitude means there is less horsepower available, even with proper carburetion. Ex pect acceleration and topspeed to be reduced at higher altitudes. To overcome operating with less power at high altitudes, your snowmobile may also require different clutch and drive line settings to avoid poor performance and rapid wear. If you plan to operate your snowmobile at an altitude different from the area where you bought your machine, be sure to consult your dealer. He can tell you if there are any changes necessary for the altitude where you plan to ride.

Caution: The drive chain gears and V-belt clutch shouldbe adjusted when operating over (3000ft)high altitude. Consult a dealer. FANBELT(VK540E) Deflection check

# 32. Long-term storage

**STORAGE.**
Long term storage, requires some preventive procedures to guard against deterioration.

**1. Cleaning.**
Thoroughly clean the machine, inside andout, to remove the corrosive salts and acids that can accumulate. Use Mud and Grease Release, oran equivalent, to loosen mud, greaseand grime. Wash with mild soap, then rinse and dry completely.

**2. Lubrication.**
Lubricate moving parts, suspension linkage and pivot points. Use the grease or lubricant specified in the MAINTENANCE section, or Lube-Z all general purpose lubricant. Proper lubrication fights corrosion while it reduces friction.

**3. Fuel system preparation.**
Add Fuel Conditioner/Stabilizer, or an equivalent, to the fuel tank to help prevent fuel oxidation, gum and varnish deposits, and to inhibit corrosion in the fuel system and carburetor. Inareas where oxygenated fuel("gasohol")is used, completely drain the fuel system. Consult your dealer.

**4. Engine.**
Proper storage of the engine is essential l to prevent costly rust and corrosion damage to internal engine components. This is more Important: than ever in those areas where oxygenated fuel("gasohol") isused, because the alcohol content in the fuel increases the chance for water to enter the engine. Use Stor-Rite Fogging Oil, or an equivalent, to protect both combustion chamber and crank- shaft from corrosion. An alternate method is to remove the airbox and squirt oil into the carburetor throats while the engine is running.

Caution: Do not attempt tostore the machine by simply starting the engine occasionally during the storage period. This can cause more harm than good! Moisture and acids form during combustion which can actually increase the chance for corr o sion damage during the storage period.

**5. Protection.**
Apply a coat of wax, such as Silicone Wax, to painted surfaces. Spray Silicone Spray, or an equivalent protectant, on the exterior of the engine onthe track, and on other metal, plastio and rubber parts.
6. Battery Remove the battery from the machine and check the fluid level. Chargethe battery. Store it in a cool, dry place that is above 0°C (32°F), but less than 30°C (90°F). Check battery condition with a hydrometer monthly, and charge as necessary.

Warning: - Never smoke or make and break connections atthe battery while charging. Sparks mayignite thebattery gas. Be sure the battery terminals are tight and that the battery vent tube is properly routed andis securely attached to thebattery.

**Do not charge battery quickly. Chargefor 10hours at1. 4amperes. Do not charge batt.**
ery quickly. Chargefor 10 hours at
1. 6 amperes.

**7. Track.**
Loosen the track, and block up the chas s is so that the track is suspended above theground.
8. Drive belt Remove the drivebelt and store sepa rately.
9. Storage Store the machine in a dry, well-venti- late d place out of direct sunlight. Puta fabric(breathable)cover over it, preferably one designed for your machine. Do not use a plastic or vinyl cover-condensation could be trapped underneath whichcould increase the chance of rusting.

text:
# 3. Powering On and Pairing the Earbuds

When the charging case is opened, the earbuds first connect to each other and then enter pairing mode.

When the earbuds are in the case, the earbud LEDs show their charging status. [Manual12_5]

When the earbuds are removed from the case, the earbud LEDs show their pairing status. [Manual12_6]

# 4. Connecting by Bluetooth

1. Open the Bluetooth settings page on your phone or device.
2. Make sure Bluetooth is turned on.
3. Select the available device named `earphones`.

Note: If the earbuds have previously been paired with a nearby device, they will automatically reconnect to that device.

[Manual12_7]

# 5. Using Multipoint Bluetooth Connection

Multipoint connection lets you connect the earbuds to up to two devices, such as a smartphone and a computer.

1. On the device already paired with the earbuds, open the Bluetooth menu and turn Bluetooth off.
2. The earbuds disconnect from that device and become available for pairing with a second device.
3. Pair the earbuds with the second device.
4. Turn Bluetooth back on for the first device.
5. The earbuds automatically reconnect to the first device.

After both devices are paired, you can use either device for music or calls.

# 6. Controlling Music and Calls

Use the multifunction buttons on the earbuds to control music playback and calls.

# 7. Using Voice Assistant, Music App, ANC, Ambient Awareness, and Low Latency Mode

To activate your phone voice assistant, press and hold the multifunction button until the first beep, then release. [earphones_01]

To activate the music app, press and hold the multifunction button until the first beep, then release. The music app resumes playback where you left off. If there was no previous session, or to play other music, tap again and the music app will play recommended songs. [earphones_02]

To turn ambient awareness and ANC modes on or off, press the left earbud. The earbud cycles through the available modes. [earphones_03]

Low Latency Mode reduces the delay inherent in Bluetooth connections. It is best for lip-sync and gaming. To turn Low Latency Mode on or off, press and hold until the second beep, then release.

section_path: 8. Pairing a New Device and Resetting the Earbuds
text:
# 8. Pairing a New Device and Resetting the Earbuds

To pair a new device, turn Bluetooth off on the currently connected phone or device. The earphones will enter pairing mode.

Alternatively, press and then press and hold either the left or right earbud to drop the current connection and enter pairing mode.

Before resetting, disconnect the earbuds from Bluetooth and remove them from the case.

To perform a factory reset, press and hold for 6 seconds. This erases all settings. [Manual12_11]

To perform a hardware reset, press and hold for 10 seconds. This restarts the earphones. Press again to power them on. [Manual12_12]

Flashing red and blue lights may appear during reset. Hardware resets are only necessary in rare cases when the earbuds lock up and become unresponsive.

section_title: 9. Using the App and Voice Control
section_path: 9. Using the App and Voice Control
text:
# 9. Using the App and Voice Control

The earphones app lets you enable hands-free voice control, customize button actions, browse and enable advanced features, and update firmware when necessary.

When the app notifies you that firmware is available, update to the latest firmware to ensure the best performance and user experience.

Once voice control is enabled in the app, say “Hey assistant” and wait for the confirmation tone. Then use a supported voice command. A second tone is heard after a successful command.

Supported commands include: “Play”, “Pause”, “Next”, “Volume Up”, “Volume Down”, “Ambient On”, “Ambient Off”, “Noise Canceling On”, “Noise Canceling Off”, “Spotify”, “Assistant”, and “End Call”.

When a call is coming in, you can also say “Accept” or “Reject” without saying “Hey assistant” first.

# 10. Safety Instructions

When using the earphones, basic safety precautions should always be followed.

[Manual12_13]

1. Read all instructions before using the earphones and charging case.
2. Do not use the product near water or place it on wet surfaces.
3. Clean only with a clean cloth.
4. Do not allow children to play with this product. It contains small parts that may create a choking hazard. Parental supervision is advised.
5. Do not expose the product to excessive heat or fire.
6. Do not expose the product to temperatures above 100°F. Keep it out of direct sunlight.
7. Do not attempt to repair the product yourself. Contact a qualified service center if service is needed.
8. Do not drop, crush, or expose the product to excessive physical force.
9. This product is not intended for commercial use.
10. When charging, keep all charging cables well ventilated. Do not keep the charging cable in contact with flammable materials such as bedding, linens, or synthetic fabrics.

# 11. Maintenance and Care

- Use a soft cloth or paper towel to clean the earphones.
- Never use harsh chemicals or detergents for cleaning.
- Make sure the earphones are dry before charging.
- When the earphones are not in use, store them in a cool, dry place.
- Never tug or yank on a cable while it is connected to the charging case.
- Connect and disconnect cables carefully.
- Never expose the earphones to high temperatures or extreme cold.
- Recycle or dispose of the earphones properly according to local laws and rules. Contact local recycling facilities or the manufacturer for more information.

# 12. Specifications

- Sweat and dustproof rating: IP55
- Battery type: lithium polymer battery
- Bluetooth version: 5.2
- Bluetooth range: 50 ft
- Earbud battery capacity: 60 mAh
- Charging case battery capacity: 600 mAh
- Earbud charging time: approximately 1 hour
- Fast charge time: 10 minutes for 2 hours of playtime
- Play time: approximately 9 hours
- Total play time with case: approximately 36 hours, because the case holds 3 additional charges

# 13. FCC Statement and RF Exposure

This equipment complies with Part 15 of the FCC Rules. Operation is subject to two conditions: the device may not cause harmful interference, and it must accept any interference received, including interference that may cause undesired operation.

The equipment has been tested and found to comply with the limits for a Class B digital device. If radio or television interference occurs, try reorienting or relocating the receiving antenna, increasing the separation between the equipment and receiver, connecting the equipment to a different circuit, or consulting a dealer or experienced radio/TV technician.

FCC RF exposure statement: The device has been evaluated to meet general RF exposure requirements and can be used in portable exposure conditions without restriction.

# 14. Warranty, Service, and Troubleshooting

Keep the manual and all relevant information for future reference.

The warranty covers the original consumer purchaser only and is not transferable. Products that fail under normal usage due to defects in material or workmanship will be repaired or replaced at no charge for parts or labor for one year.

The warranty does not cover damage or malfunctions not resulting from defects in material or workmanship. This includes damage from abnormal use, repair by unauthorized parties, tampering, modification, or accident.

To obtain warranty service or troubleshooting information, contact the manufacturer for problem determination and service procedures. Proof of purchase, such as a bill of sale or receipted invoice, must be presented to obtain service. Package and send any defective product with a dated proof of purchase, a written explanation of the problem, and a valid return address to the authorized service center. Do not include other items or accessories with the defective product.

text:
# 1. 产品说明与使用前须知

本说明书适用于 VR 头显及其配套硬件。使用本产品前，请仔细阅读本说明书及配套硬件的相关手册，并遵守所有警告、注意事项和安装说明。请妥善保管本说明书，以备日后参考。

PS VR 需与主机及摄像头配合使用，可提供沉浸式虚拟现实体验。摄像头会捕捉 VR 头显的位置、角度和动作，让您能够更直接地与游戏和应用互动。使用前，请务必将主机系统软件更新至最新版本。

VR 头显不适用于 12 岁以下儿童。若您感到疲劳、头晕、头昏、恶心、身体不适，或处于醉酒、服药状态，或运动感、平衡感受损，请勿使用 PS VR。若您患有严重疾病，使用 PS VR 前请咨询医生。

初次使用虚拟现实内容时，可能需要一定适应时间。建议首次使用时缩短使用时间，并在使用过程中根据身体状况适当休息。通常建议每游玩 1 小时休息 15 分钟；观看虚拟现实内容时，休息时长和频率因人而异，请休息至不适感完全消退后再继续使用。

section_title: 2. 健康警告与立即停止使用的情况
section_path: 2. 健康警告与立即停止使用的情况
text:
# 2. 健康警告与立即停止使用的情况

若您或您的孩子出现以下任何健康问题或症状，请立即停止使用，并咨询医生。仅在医生许可后方可继续使用：

- 头晕、头痛、恶心、疲劳或类似晕动症的症状。
- 视觉异常、视力模糊、眼睛或肌肉抽搐。
- 意识丧失、方向障碍、癫痫发作。
- 不自主运动、抽搐，或身体任何部位出现不适或疼痛。
- 眼睛、耳朵、手、手臂、脚或其他部位出现异常不适。

部分用户可能会出现晕动症、恶心、方向障碍、视力模糊或其他不适。若出现此类情况，请立即停止使用并摘下 VR 头显。使用后若仍感到不适，请休息，并避免从事需要良好视力、平衡感或协调能力的活动，直至症状完全消失。

当您疲劳或需要睡眠时，请勿使用 PS VR。请勿在可能发生震动或其他不稳定的环境中使用 PS VR。

section_title: 3. 光敏性癫痫与光线刺激风险
section_path: 3. 光敏性癫痫与光线刺激风险
text:
# 3. 光敏性癫痫与光线刺激风险

若您患有癫痫或曾有癫痫发作史，游玩前请咨询医生。部分人在接触闪烁灯光或其他光线刺激时，可能会出现眼睛酸痛、视觉异常、偏头痛、肌肉抽搐、痉挛、昏厥、意识丧失或方向障碍。

在电视屏幕上观看或游玩电子游戏时，也可能出现类似症状。若游玩期间出现上述任何症状，请立即停止使用并咨询医生。仅在医生许可后方可继续游玩。

# 4. 游玩区域与使用环境

佩戴 VR 头显会限制您对真实环境的视野，且 VR 头显无法检测障碍物。使用前，请检查并清理大于游玩区域的活动空间，移除墙壁、楼梯、家具、宠物、他人或其他可能导致碰撞、绊倒或干扰操作的障碍物。

请在游玩区域内使用 PS VR。游玩区域的高度取决于摄像头的捕捉范围，游玩区域的宽度和深度请根据系统设置界面进行调整。[Manual38_0]
[Manual38_0 图号描述：图示为游戏区域空间设置示意图。画面中心是一个矩形地面区域，内部印有黑色文字“Play Area”，区域中央绘制有一个坐在椅子上的人形轮廓。右上方安装有一个黑色设备，标注文字为“PlayStation®Camera”。从相机位置延伸出锥形视野覆盖该矩形区域。图中通过尺寸线和箭头标注了多处距离数值：矩形区域的短边宽度标注为“Approx. 1.9 m”，长边长度标注为“Approx. 3.0 m”；相机与矩形区域近端边缘的距离标注为“Approx. 0.7 m”；在相机右侧的水平基准线上，标注有“0 m”以及下方一段距离“Approx. 0.6 m”。]

按照 PS VR 设置界面的指示调整摄像头位置及角度，使您处于 VR 模式的最佳游玩位置，也就是游玩区域中央。若使用 VR 模式时超出游玩区域，头显屏幕将出现警告。

若 VR 头显未被正确检测，请长按控制器上的按键，然后从弹出的快捷菜单中选择 [调整 VR] > [确认位置]，再调整摄像头位置及角度。

佩戴 VR 头显时，请尽量保持坐姿并停留在游玩区域中央，切勿随意走动。避免头部、四肢或身体做出剧烈或过度动作。若应用程序要求您佩戴头显时站立，请严格遵循应用程序的指示。

开始游玩前，请检查 VR 头显线缆是否缠绕在身体或四肢上，并在游玩过程中经常检查。

section_title: 5. 安全使用与日常操作注意事项
section_path: 5. 安全使用与日常操作注意事项
text:
# 5. 安全使用与日常操作注意事项

请勿损坏电源线及电源适配器。连接前，请检查接口是否没有灰尘、细小杂物或异物。

请勿抓着线缆甩动 VR 头显或电源适配器。请勿在产品上放置物品、投掷或摔落产品，或使其遭受强烈物理撞击。

待头显上的追踪灯熄灭后，再取下 VR 头显或拔下头显连接线。灯光亮起时取下或拔线可能导致设备故障。

请将本产品放置在幼儿接触不到的地方。幼儿可能吞咽细小零件、拉扯线缆导致处理器单元或 VR 头显坠落，或将线缆缠绕在身上，从而造成人身伤害、意外或设备故障。

雷雨天气时，请勿触碰电源线、电源适配器或处理器单元。请勿让液体或细小颗粒进入产品内部，例如接口或通风口。若发生此类情况，请立即停止使用并断开电源。

请勿将产品暴露在灰尘、烟雾或蒸汽中。灰尘等物质可能引发火灾或触电。

产品开机时，避免身体长时间接触处理器单元、电源适配器或通风口排出的空气。长时间接触可能导致低温烫伤。低温烫伤是指皮肤长时间接触温度相对较低、约 40°C 及以上物体所造成的烫伤。

若 VR 头显、立体声耳机或另售的立体声头戴设备导致皮肤不适，请停止使用。若皮肤不适症状未消退，请就医。

请勿在产品上使用溶剂或其他化学药剂。避免橡胶或乙烯基材料与产品长时间接触，以防止产品外壳老化或变色。

# 6. 听力保护与耳机使用

以高音量使用头显或耳机可能导致永久性听力损伤。请将音量调至安全水平。随着时间推移，过大的音量可能听起来正常，但实际上会损害您的听力。

若您出现耳鸣、耳部不适或听觉模糊，请停止聆听并检查听力。音量越大，听力受损越快。

为保护听力，请缩短高音量使用头显或耳机的时间，不要为了隔绝环境噪音而调高音量。若听不到身边人说话，请调低音量。

在特别干燥的环境下使用头显或耳机时，耳朵可能偶尔感受到短暂轻微的静电触击。这是人体积聚静电所致，并非头显或耳机故障。

section_title: 7. 佩戴 VR 头显与屏幕注意事项
section_path: 7. 佩戴 VR 头显与屏幕注意事项
text:
# 7. 佩戴 VR 头显与屏幕注意事项

使用时正确佩戴 VR 头显非常重要。有关佩戴头显的说明，请前往系统功能界面查看。请勿将调节旋钮拧得过紧。

调节镜罩位置后，您可以佩戴眼镜使用 PS VR。请勿过度推入或拉出镜罩。请定期检查产品佩戴状态，确保佩戴正确。

屏幕特定位置可能出现黑色暗点像素或常亮像素。此类斑点属于屏幕正常现象，并非系统故障。屏幕采用高精度技术制造，但每个屏幕仍可能出现极少数暗点、常亮像素、色彩不均或亮度不均。

请保持 VR 头显的附着传感器无遮挡。若附着传感器被遮挡，取下头显时屏幕可能不会自动关闭。若屏幕长时间显示同一画面，可能导致画面残留并形成永久性残影。

section_title: 8. 禁止拆卸、异常处理与高温提示
section_path: 8. 禁止拆卸、异常处理与高温提示
text:
# 8. 禁止拆卸、异常处理与高温提示

请按照本说明书指示使用本产品及配件。未经授权，不得对本产品进行拆解、改装，或分析其电路结构。拆卸将导致产品保修失效，并可能造成火灾、触电或故障风险。

若 PS VR 从寒冷环境直接移至温暖环境，产品内部可能结露。在这种情况下，产品可能无法正常工作。请关闭产品并断开电源线，待水分完全蒸发后再使用，这可能需要数小时。若产品仍无法正常工作，请联系 PlayStation 客户支持。

若产品异常或无响应，请长按 VR 头显线控上的电源键至少 7 秒以强制关机，然后重新开机。若问题仍然存在，请重启主机系统。

若处理器单元内部温度升高，屏幕将显示提示信息。此时，请关闭系统并静置一段时间。待处理器单元冷却后，将其移至通风良好的位置，再继续使用。请勿遮挡处理器单元通风口，也不要在封闭橱柜等易积热的环境中使用本产品。

section_title: 9. 电源适配器、电源线与存放条件
section_path: 9. 电源适配器、电源线与存放条件
text:
# 9. 电源适配器、电源线与存放条件

使用便于插拔的电源插座，以便需要时可快速断开电源线。若产品出现异常运行、发出异常声音或气味，或出现过热发烫，请立即停止使用，断开电源线及其他所有线缆。

处理器单元状态指示灯为红色时，才可拔下电源线。指示灯为白色或闪烁红色时拔线可能导致故障。

请勿使用产品标配以外的电源适配器或电源线。标配电源适配器及电源线专为本产品设计，不可用于其他产品；其他适配器或电源线也不可用于本产品。违反此注意事项可能导致产品过热，引发火灾或触电。

连接好 HDMI 线缆后，再将产品电源线插入电源。湿手请勿触碰电源插头。请勿用布覆盖使用中的电源适配器，否则可能积热，引发火灾或故障。清洁或长期不使用产品时，请拔下电源线。请勿将电源线连接至电压变压器或逆变器。

请勿将产品或配件置于高温、高湿或阳光直射的环境中。请勿使用烘干机等厨房或加热设备烘烤产品，否则可能引发火灾、人身伤害或故障。请勿将产品或配件放置在不稳定、倾斜或易震动的平面上。

section_title: 10. VR 设置与儿童使用限制
section_path: 10. VR 设置与儿童使用限制
text:
# 10. VR 设置与儿童使用限制

如需配置 VR 设置，请前往系统功能界面，然后选择（设置） > [设备] > [VR]。这些设置仅当 VR 连接至主机时可用。

也可以长按控制器上的按键弹出快捷菜单，配置部分 VR 设置。有关 VR 设置的更多信息，请参阅主机用户指南：在功能界面中选择（设置） > [用户指南]。

系统包含家长或监护人可按需配置的设置，以限制儿童使用本产品。如需限制使用，请前往系统功能界面，选择（设置） > [家长控制] > [限制功能使用] > [VR] > [不允许]。

配置家长控制设置需要家长控制密码。所设限制适用于主机所有用户。

# 11. VR 头显部件名称

VR 头显正面部件包括前侧追踪灯、后侧灯光、前侧头托、后侧头托、AUX 接口、HDMI 接口、镜罩、线缆挂钩、麦克风、遮光罩、镜罩调节键和前侧追踪灯。[vr_01] [vr_02]

灯光状态如下：

- 蓝色：已开机。
- 所有灯蓝色：VR 模式。
- 灯灭：已关机。

VR 头显后侧部件包括头带、附着传感器、镜片、调节旋钮、头带释放键、后侧追踪灯、线控、立体声耳机插孔、电源键、麦克风静音键、音量加键和音量减键。[vr_03] [vr_04]

section_title: 12. 处理器单元与立体声耳机部件名称
section_path: 12. 处理器单元与立体声耳机部件名称
text:
# 12. 处理器单元与立体声耳机部件名称

处理器单元正面包括状态指示灯、AUX 端口和 HDMI 输出端口。[Manual38_1]

状态指示灯含义如下：

- 白色：已开机。
- 红色：待机模式。

处理器单元背面包括 HDMI 电视端口、HDMI PS4 端口、USB 端口、DC IN 12V 接口和通风口。[Manual38_2]

立体声耳机的主要部件为耳塞。[Manual38_3]

# 13. 更换耳塞

立体声耳机出厂时已安装 M 号耳塞。您可以根据佩戴情况更换为 S 号或 L 号耳塞，以获得更贴合的佩戴效果。

取下耳塞时，旋转耳塞后将其拔下即可。[Manual38_4]

安装耳塞时，请将耳塞牢固装回耳机，防止使用过程中意外脱落。

# 14. 保养与清洁

清洁前，请先拔下电源线并断开其他所有线缆。请勿使用溶剂或其他化学药剂清洁产品外壳，也不要使用经化学处理的清洁布擦拭产品。

处理器单元外壳、VR 头显外壳、头托和接口若有污渍，请用柔软干布擦拭。若处理器单元、电源线或其他部件上的接口变脏，可能导致信号传输异常。若耳机或头显接口不洁，还可能出现噪音或声音中断。

镜片只能使用专用柔软干布擦拭。请勿使用纸巾等非镜片专用纸质产品。长时间接触水或灰尘可能损坏镜片并缩短其使用寿命。

遮光罩可以从 VR 头显上取下并用水清洗。清洗后请用软布完全擦干，再装回头显。重新安装时，将遮光罩上的凸点与头显上的 13 个孔对齐。[Manual38_5]

通风口如有灰尘，可使用吸尘器等工具清除。

耳塞可以从立体声耳机上取下，用中性洗涤剂手洗。清洗后请用软布完全擦干，再装回耳机。取下耳塞的说明请参阅“更换耳塞”。

section_title: 15. 英国用户、能效信息与废弃处理
section_path: 15. 英国用户、能效信息与废弃处理
text:
# 15. 英国用户、能效信息与废弃处理

为安全与方便起见，部分地区设备可能配备成型插头。若需更换插头内的保险丝，请按照当地适用的电气安全要求进行处理。

有关欧盟（EU）第 801/2013 号法规中生态设计要求的相关信息，请访问官方能效信息页面。

在欧洲及土耳其地区，当您在电气产品或包装上看到废弃电气产品符号时，表示相关电气产品不应作为普通生活垃圾处理。请依照适用法律法规，通过授权回收设施进行处理。

购买同类新产品时，也可将废弃电气产品交由零售商免费回收。在欧盟国家，较大型零售商也可能免费回收小型废弃电子产品。请咨询当地零售商是否提供相关回收服务。

正确处理废弃产品有助于节约自然资源，并提升电气废弃物处理的环保标准。本产品及其部件由金属和塑料制成。废弃时，请遵守当地法规妥善处理此类材料。

# 1. Product Overview and Features

[Manual39_0]

Read this manual thoroughly before operating the washing machine, and keep it for future reference.

This washing machine is designed for household laundry use. It includes the following main features:

- Powerful washing with a large pulsator for more even washing.
- Three-way lint filter to efficiently collect lint during washing.
- Normal and Soft wash selector for different fabric types and washing needs.

# 2. Safety Cautions

[Manual39_1]

Make sure the washing machine is properly grounded. To avoid electric shock, use a suitable grounding connection. Do not ground the washer to gas pipes or telephone lines, as this may cause explosion or lightning-strike hazards.

Do not put your hands into the spin dryer basket while it is spinning. Your fingers may be caught by the spinning laundry and injured.

[washing_machine1_02]

Never allow children to operate or play with the washer. Children playing near or inside the washer may accidentally fall into the washing tub.

[washing_machine1_01]

Disconnect the power cord from the power supply after use.

When the washing machine is installed on a carpeted floor, make sure the ventilation openings are not obstructed by the carpet.

If the supply cord is damaged, it must be replaced only by an authorized technician appointed by the manufacturer, because special-purpose tools are required.

To avoid overfilling and damage, the appliance must be filled while the operator is present and with moderate water-supply pressure only.

# 3. Operating Precautions

Do not use excessively hot water. Water at 50°C or higher may deform or damage plastic parts and may also deform or discolor clothing.

Before washing, empty all pockets. Nails, pins, coins, or other hard objects may damage the washer or clothing.

If the water pressure is too high, close the water tap slightly.

Before spinning, make sure the inner cover is placed over the laundry. This helps prevent laundry from being thrown out and damaged.

Close the wash tub lid to avoid water splashing.

Never splash water on the control panel.

# 4. Parts Description

[Manual39_2]

Main parts of the washing machine include:

- Water drain option hose with pump
- Overflow filter
- Lint filter
- Wash tub
- Wash tub lid
- Spin dryer lid
- Spin dryer basket
- Spin dryer hatch
- Power cord
- Drain filter
- Earth wire
- Water drain hose without pump
- Pulsator

Keep the wash tub lid closed during washing and spinning.

When the spin dryer lid is opened while the spin basket is spinning, the brake system stops the basket.

The shape of the power plug may differ from the illustration.

# 5. Control Panel

[Manual39_3]

The control panel contains the following controls:

1. Wash Selector: Selects the wash action.
2. Wash Timer: Sets the washing time from 1 to 15 minutes.
3. Cycle Selector: Selects Washing/Rinsing or Draining.
4. Spin Dry Timer: Sets the spin time from 1 to 5 minutes, or from 1 to 10 minutes depending on the model.
5. Water Selector: During washing, select Wash. During spin rinsing, select Spin.

# 6. Washing Procedure

[Manual39_4]

Before starting washing, check the following:

1. Connect the water supply hose and open the water tap.
2. For models without a drain pump, lay the drain hose down toward a sinkhole.
3. For models with a drain pump, place the drain hose in a sink or bath.
4. Connect the power cord to the power supply outlet.

Set the Wash Selector knob to the desired mode.

[Manual39_5]

Set the Water Selector knob to Wash.

[Manual39_6]

Set the Cycle Selector knob to Wash/Rinse. For drain-pump models, set it to Wash.

[Manual39_7]

Fill the wash tub with water and add detergent.

[Manual39_8]

Load the laundry into the wash tub and fill water to the high water level.

[Manual39_9]

Set the Wash Timer for 1 to 15 minutes.

[Manual39_10]

After washing, set the Cycle Selector knob to Drain to drain the water.

# 7. Spin Drying

[Manual39_11]

Transfer the clothes into the spin basket and arrange them evenly.

[Manual39_12]

Attach the safety cover and close the inner lid.

[Manual39_13]

Close the spin dryer lid.

[Manual39_14]

Set the Spin Dry Timer for 1 to 5 minutes, or for 1 to 10 minutes depending on the model.

[Manual39_15]

# 8. Rinsing

[Manual39_16]

Set the Cycle Selector knob to Wash/Rinse. For drain-pump models, set it to Wash.

Supply the proper amount of water. Do not allow the water to overflow from the top of the washing tub.

[Manual39_17]

Set the Wash Timer for 2 to 3 minutes.

[Manual39_18]

Drain the water by setting the Cycle Selector knob to Drain.

Repeat the rinse cycle 2 to 3 times, or until the drained water is clean.

# 9. Overflow Rinse

[Manual39_19]

Keep supplying water during the overflow rinse. Adjust the water pressure so that the amount of water supplied does not exceed the amount of water being drained.

[Manual39_20]

Set the Wash Timer for 6 to 8 minutes.

[Manual39_21]

As soon as the Wash Timer shuts off, turn off the water tap.

[Manual39_22]

Set the Cycle Selector knob to Drain.

# 10. Additional Rinse

[Manual39_23]

Use the additional rinse when extra rinsing is needed after the normal rinse cycle.

1. Add clean water to the wash tub.
2. Set the Cycle Selector knob to Wash/Rinse.
3. Set the Wash Timer for a short rinse cycle.
4. Drain the water after rinsing.
5. Repeat if necessary until the laundry is properly rinsed.

# 11. Installation Environment

[Manual39_24]
[Manual39_24 description: The figure is black-and-white schematic diagram, shows a and. top is circular, upper center has. lower center connection drain hose and. right side connection hose, under. left side under hose. image lower right has a component and hose. image left side has a arrow, labeled on left side hose, text shows is "70~80cm".]

Leave at least 15 cm of space between the washer and the wall.

Place the washer on a sturdy, flat surface. If the washer is placed on an uneven or weak surface, noise or vibration may occur. The allowable inclination is about 2°.

Do not install the washer near water. Do not place the washer in steamy rooms or where it is directly exposed to rain. Moisture may damage the electrical insulation and cause an electric shock hazard.

Avoid direct sunlight and heating devices. Plastic and electrical components can be affected by direct heat, so do not place the washer near heaters, boilers, or similar heat sources.

For pump models, install the drain hose about 70 to 80 cm above the ground.

section_title: 12. Connecting the Drain Hose and Mounting the Legs
section_path: 12. Connecting the Drain Hose and Mounting the Legs
text:
# 12. Connecting the Drain Hose and Mounting the Legs

[Manual39_25]

To connect the drain hose:

1. Before connecting the drain hose, remove the cover from the drain hole.
2. Press the joint ring and insert the drain hose in the drain direction.

[Manual39_26]

To mount the legs:

1. Lay the washer down with its back facing downward.
2. Insert the four legs into the leg-mounting sections at the base corners of the main body.
3. Insert the claw of each leg into the square hole of the leg-mounting section.
4. Push each leg in the direction shown in the figure until it clicks into place.

# 13. Cleaning the Machine

[Manual39_27]

To clean the lint filter, push it down and pull it out after washing if lint or debris has collected in the filter. Remove the collected lint and rinse the filter net.

[Manual39_28]

If draining is incomplete, disassemble the drain filter with a Phillips screwdriver and remove lint from the filter.

[Manual39_29]

To clean the overflow filter, pull the upper side of the overflow filter with two fingers into the hole and remove it in the direction shown by the arrow.

To clean the wash tub, fill the wash tub with water to the proper level, then drain the water while operating the wash cycle for 1 to 2 minutes. Keep the wash tub lid closed during this operation.

To clean the washer body, wipe stains from the cabinet and control panel with a soft cloth. Do not use benzene, thinner, cleanser, wax, or a brush. These may damage painted surfaces or plastic parts.

# 14. Laundry Guide

[Manual39_30]
[Manual39_30 description: The image shows a contains columns table, used for different settings. table header from left to right in order are "KINDS OF CLOTHING" (), "WASHING TIME" (time) and "WASHING SELECTION" (select). table content is divided into rows data: first row columns "Extremely solid heavy fabric", corresponds to time "10 to 15 minutes", select is "NORMAL"; second row columns "Linen, cotton, etc. ", corresponds to time "8 to 10 minutes", select is "NORMAL" (cell front rows). third row columns "Ordinary clothes (underwear, etc)", corresponds to time "7 minutes", select is "SOFT"; fourth row columns "Slightly soiled synthetic fiber", corresponds to time "2 to 5 minutes"; fifth row columns "100% wool, mixed wool knitting, thin synthetic fiber with tags indicating hand washing", corresponds to time "2 to 5 minutes". where, "SOFT" select cell rear rows.]

Use the washing time chart as a guide for choosing the proper wash time according to fabric type and soil level.

[Manual39_31]
[Manual39_31 description: The image shows a time and type corresponds to relationship table. table is divided into columns, columns table header text is "TIME", columns table header text is "TYPE OF LAUNDRY". table main body contains rows data: first row left side is "1min. ", right side is "Thin(synthetic fiber)"; second row left side is "1~2min. ", right side is "wool"; third row left side is "3~5min. ", right side is "cotton"; fourth row left side is "5min. ", right side is "thick(cotton)". table consists of black separated by lines cell.]

Use the spin dry time chart as a guide for choosing the proper spin time according to laundry type and amount.

[Manual39_32]
[Manual39_32 description: The image shows a two- columns table. table header left side text is "AMOUNT OF DETERGENT", right side text is "WATER LEVEL". table contains rows data corresponds to relationship: first row left side is "30 g", right side is "Low (30l)"; second row left side is "40 g", right side is "Mid (40l)"; third row left side is "50 g", right side is "High (50l)".]

Use an average amount of detergent unless the detergent package gives specific instructions. Adjust the detergent amount according to the type and amount of fabric.

# 15. Maintenance

[Manual39_33]

When loading laundry into the spin basket, press the laundry evenly and place the safety cover into the spin basket drum as shown.

[Manual39_34]

If clothing falls between the spin basket and the tub, follow these steps:

1. For safety, unplug the power supply plug from the socket.
2. Remove the screws from the spin dryer hatch.
3. The spin dryer hatch is fixed to the rim by concave and convex parts at two locations. Release these parts and pull up the spin dryer hatch to remove it.
4. Remove the clothing.
5. Close the spin dryer hatch. Push the hatch firmly until the catch at the front is securely engaged.

# 16. Troubleshooting

[Manual39_35]
[Manual39_35 description: The image shows a troubleshooting table, is divided into two left and right section, section contains "TROUBLE" (fault) and "CHECK POINT" (check) columns. left side section contains rows content: first row fault is "The washer does not work. ", check is "Is the laundry overloaded?"; third row fault is "Incomplete spinning", check is "Are the laundry arranged evenly?". right side section contains rows content: first row fault is "Incomplete draining", check is "Is the filter clogged with lint?"; second row fault is "The spin dryer basket will not run. ", corresponds to check contains, where rear front has black triangle symbol: is "Is the spin dryer lid closed completely?", is "► Are laundry(socks,etc. )falling out of the spin dryer basket and clinging to the axle?", is "► See "To pick out... " on page 6. ".]

If the washer does not operate correctly, check the basic items below before requesting service:

- Make sure the power plug is connected properly.
- Make sure the water tap is open.
- Make sure the drain hose is positioned correctly.
- Check whether laundry is unevenly arranged in the spin basket.
- Check whether the lint filter or drain filter is clogged.
- Check whether the washer is placed on a stable and level surface.

If the problem continues after these checks, contact an authorized service technician.

# 17. Specifications

Refer to the product label and the specifications section of the original manual for model-specific ratings, dimensions, and capacities.

section_path: 1. Owner Information, Manual Conventions, Identification Numbers, Emissions, and Labels
text:
# 1. Owner Information, Manual Conventions, Identification Numbers, Emissions, and Labels

This 2005 WaveRunner Owner’s/Operator’s Manual contains the information needed for proper operation, maintenance, and care of the watercraft. Read and understand the manual before operating the watercraft. Keep the manual with the watercraft if it is sold.

If you have questions about operation or maintenance, consult a Jet Ski dealer. Because the manufacturer continually improves its products, the actual watercraft may differ slightly from the descriptions and specifications in this manual.

Important manual terms:

- Warning: Failure to follow warning instructions could result in severe injury or death to the operator, passenger, bystanders, or a person inspecting or repairing the watercraft.
- Caution: Indicates special precautions that must be taken to avoid damage to the watercraft.
- Note: Provides key information that makes procedures easier or clearer.

Record the identification numbers in a safe place for ordering spare parts and for theft records.

Primary Identification Number (PRI-ID):

[Manual20_0]

The PRI-ID number is stamped on a label attached inside the engine compartment.

[jetski_01]

Hull Identification Number (HIN):

[Manual20_1]

The HIN is stamped on a plate attached to the hull on the aft starboard, or right, side.

[jetski_02]

Engine serial number:

[Manual20_2]

The engine serial number is stamped on a label attached to the engine unit.

[jetski_03]

This engine conforms to 2005 U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) regulations for marine SI engines.

[Manual20_3]

The emission control certificate label is attached to the electrical box and the exhaust side of the crankcase.

[Manual20_4]

[Manual20_5]

The manufactured date label is attached to the electrical box and the exhaust side of the crankcase.

[Manual20_6]

Read all important labels before operating the watercraft. Maintain or replace warning, caution, and instruction labels as necessary.

section_title: 2. General Safety Requirements and Operator Limits
section_path: 2. General Safety Requirements and Operator Limits
text:
# 2. General Safety Requirements and Operator Limits

Safe use and operation depend on proper riding techniques, common sense, good judgment, and operator skill. Before operating the watercraft, read the Owner’s/Operator’s Manual, Riding Practice Guide, Riding Instruction card, and all warning and caution labels. Watch the Basic Orientation Video supplied with the watercraft when possible.

Never allow anyone to operate the watercraft until they have read the required materials and understand the controls and warnings.

[Manual20_14]

Operator and passenger limits:

- The recommended minimum operator age is 16 years.
- Adults must supervise minors.
- Know and follow operator age and training requirements for your state.
- A boating safety course is recommended and may be required locally.
- The watercraft is designed to carry the operator and one passenger only.
- Never exceed the maximum load or allow more than 2 persons to ride at one time.
- Maximum load is 160 kg (353 lb), including cargo, operator, and passenger.
- Do not operate with a passenger until you have considerable practice and experience riding alone.

[Manual20_15]

Operating with a passenger requires more skill. Become familiar with the handling characteristics of the watercraft before attempting difficult maneuvers.

# 3. Cruising Limitations and Riding Environment

Operate defensively and stay alert at all times.

[Manual20_16]

Cruising requirements:

- Constantly scan for people, objects, swimmers, and other watercraft.
- Watch for conditions that limit visibility or block your view of others.
- Operate at safe speeds and maintain a safe distance from people, objects, and other watercraft.
- Do not follow directly behind other watercraft or boats.
- Do not spray or splash people.
- Avoid sharp turns and maneuvers that make it difficult for others to avoid you or understand your path.
- Avoid submerged objects and shallow water.
- Ride within your limits and avoid aggressive maneuvers that increase the risk of loss of control, ejection, or collision.
- Do not operate in rough water, bad weather, or poor visibility.
- Check weather forecasts and prevailing conditions before riding.
- Do not ride farther than swimming distance from shore unless another boat or watercraft is nearby at a safe distance.

[Manual20_17]

Do not operate in water less than 60 cm (2 ft) deep. Shallow water increases the risk of hitting submerged objects.

This is a high-performance boat, not a toy. Sharp turns, jumping wakes, and jumping waves can increase the risk of back or spinal injury, paralysis, facial injury, and broken bones. Do not jump wakes or waves.

[Manual20_18]

The watercraft is not equipped with lighting required for night operation. Do not operate it after sunset or before dawn because of the risk of collision.

section_title: 4. Rider Protective Gear, Health, and Required Conduct
section_path: 4. Rider Protective Gear, Health, and Required Conduct
text:
# 4. Rider Protective Gear, Health, and Required Conduct

All riders must wear a Coast Guard-approved personal flotation device (PFD) suitable for personal watercraft use.

Wear protective clothing. Severe internal injuries can occur if water is forced into body cavities due to falling into the water or being near the jet thrust nozzle. Normal swimwear does not provide adequate protection. All riders must wear a wetsuit bottom or equivalent protective clothing such as thick, tightly woven, sturdy, snug-fitting apparel. Spandex or bicycle-shorts-style fabrics are not equivalent protection.

[Manual20_19]

Eye protection is recommended to keep wind, water, and glare out of your eyes. Use eyewear retaining straps designed to float if the eyewear falls into the water. Footwear and gloves are recommended.

A helmet may protect against some impacts, but it may also create hazards in personal watercraft use. Falling into the water while wearing a helmet can cause “bucketing,” where water catches the helmet and strains the neck. This may cause choking, severe neck injury, permanent injury, or death. A helmet may also reduce vision or hearing, distract the rider, or increase fatigue. Consider your riding environment, style, ability, traffic, and water conditions before deciding whether to wear one. If you wear a helmet, choose one designed for personal watercraft use when possible. For closed-course competition, follow the race organization’s helmet rules.

[Manual20_20]

Additional requirements:

- Never operate the watercraft after consuming alcohol or taking drugs.
- Always perform the pre-operation checks before operating.
- The operator and passenger must keep both feet in the footwell while the watercraft is moving.
- Do not carry a child whose feet cannot reach the footwell floor.
- The passenger must hold firmly to the operator.
- Consult a doctor before riding if you are pregnant or in poor health.
- Do not modify the watercraft. Modifications may reduce safety and reliability and may make the watercraft unsafe or illegal.

[Manual20_21]

Traffic and swimmer awareness:

- Scan carefully for swimmers and stay away from swimming areas.
- Avoid being hit by another boat by watching for traffic at all times.
- Maintain a safe distance from boats and watercraft.
- Watch for ski ropes and fishing lines.
- Obey the Rules of the Road and check behind you before turning.

[Manual20_22]

section_title: 5. Recommended Equipment, Hazard Information, and Jet Propulsion Safety
section_path: 5. Recommended Equipment, Hazard Information, and Jet Propulsion Safety
text:
# 5. Recommended Equipment, Hazard Information, and Jet Propulsion Safety

Carry the following equipment on board:

- Sound-signaling device, such as a whistle.
- Visual distress signal, such as a USCG-approved pyrotechnic device in a waterproof container, or a mirror for emergency signaling.
- Watch to monitor riding time.
- Towline for towing a disabled watercraft in an emergency.

[Manual20_23]

Hazard information:

- When transporting or storing the watercraft, always place the fuel cock knob in the OFF position. Otherwise, gasoline may overflow from the carburetor.
- Never start or run the engine for any length of time in an enclosed area. Exhaust fumes contain carbon monoxide, a colorless and odorless gas that can cause loss of consciousness and death.
- Always operate the watercraft in an open area.

Jet propulsion characteristics:

- Jet thrust turns the watercraft.
- Releasing the throttle completely produces only minimum thrust.
- At speeds above trolling, steering ability decreases rapidly without throttle.
- Once engine speed slows, the watercraft will not respond to handlebar input until throttle is applied again or the watercraft reaches trolling speed.
- Stop the engine and remove the clip from the engine shut-off switch before clearing debris or weeds from the jet intake.

[Manual20_24]

The watercraft is water-jet propelled. The jet pump is directly connected to the engine, so jet thrust can produce movement whenever the engine is running. There is no neutral position.

Keep away from the intake grate while the engine is on. Long hair, loose clothing, and PFD straps can become entangled in moving parts, causing severe injury or drowning. Never insert any object into the jet thrust nozzle while the engine is running; contact with rotating jet pump parts could cause severe injury or death.

[Manual20_25]

section_title: 6. Rules of the Road and Responsible Riding
section_path: 6. Rules of the Road and Responsible Riding
text:
# 6. Rules of the Road and Responsible Riding

A Jet Ski watercraft is legally considered a powerboat and must be operated according to the rules and regulations of the waterway. Waterway rules are similar in purpose to road rules and are enforced by the United States Coast Guard and local agencies.

The rules in this manual are condensed for convenience. Consult local Coast Guard Auxiliary, Department of Motor Vehicles, or local boating authorities for the full rules for your riding area.

Key right-of-way concepts:

- The stand-on vessel has the right-of-way and should maintain course and speed unless avoiding an immediate collision.
- The give-way vessel must take positive and timely action to stay out of the way.
- If collision appears unavoidable, neither vessel has the right-of-way; both must avoid the collision.

When encountering vessels, the three main collision situations are meeting, crossing, and overtaking.

[Manual20_26]

Meeting: If you meet another power vessel head-on and there is a risk of collision, neither has the right-of-way. Both vessels should alter course. Keep the other vessel on your port, or left, side when possible.

[Manual20_27]

Crossing: When two power-driven vessels cross close enough to risk collision, the vessel with the other on its starboard, or right, side must keep out of the way. If the other vessel is on your right, you are the give-way vessel. If it is on your left, you should maintain course and speed if the other vessel properly gives way.

[Manual20_28]

Overtaking: If you are passing another vessel, you are the give-way vessel and must stay out of its way until clear. If another vessel is passing you, maintain course and speed so it can steer around you.

Other special situations:

- In narrow channels, keep to the right when safe and practical.
- When approaching bends where visibility is obstructed, a power-driven vessel should sound a prolonged whistle blast of four to six seconds. Carry a portable air horn for these waters.
- Fishing vessels using nets, lines, or trawls generally have the right-of-way, although they cannot block narrow channels. Vessels with trolling lines are not considered fishing vessels under these rules.
- Sailing vessels should normally be given the right-of-way, with exceptions when they are overtaking, near fishing vessels, or in narrow channels where they would hamper a power-driven vessel.
- Learn buoy and marker systems before riding in unfamiliar waters. “Red right returning” means red buoys are passed on your starboard side when returning from open water into a harbor.

[Manual20_29]

Boating safety information may be obtained from the United States Coast Guard, the National Association of State Boating Law Administrators, local Power Squadrons, and online boating safety courses.

Ride responsibly. Respect other people, shore homes, fishermen, swimmers, populated beaches, wildlife areas, and nesting areas. Ride slowly when travel through sensitive areas is unavoidable. Do not litter. Do not refuel or add oil where spills could damage the environment. Remove the watercraft from the water and move it away from shore before refueling.

section_title: 7. Main Components, Storage Compartments, and Fire Extinguisher
section_path: 7. Main Components, Storage Compartments, and Fire Extinguisher
text:
# 7. Main Components, Storage Compartments, and Fire Extinguisher

Main exterior and hull components include handlebars, fuel tank filler cap, rope hole, footwell, intake grate, speed sensor, cooling water pilot outlet, bow eye, front storage compartment, hood, jet intake, handgrip, seat, glove compartment, and adjustable sponsons.

[Manual20_30]

[Manual20_31]

[Manual20_32]

Controls and engine-related components include the engine shut-off cord, throttle lever, choke lever, oil tank filler cap, fuel cock knob, stern drain plugs, jet thrust nozzle, ride plate, engine stop switch, clip, QSTS selector, engine shut-off switch, start switch, and multifunction information center.

[Manual20_33]

Engine compartment components include spark plugs, spark plug caps, electrical box, flush hose connector, spark plug lead, muffler, fuel filter, fuel tank, oil tank, battery, fire extinguisher container, and water separator.

[Manual20_34]

Storage compartments:

- Make sure all storage compartments are secured before operating.
- Storage compartments are not waterproof. Place manuals and items that must remain dry inside a waterproof bag.

Front storage compartment:

[Manual20_63]

To open the front storage compartment, push the hood latch down and open the hood.

[Manual20_64]

[Manual20_65]

The front storage compartment can be removed to access the engine compartment.

Front storage compartment capacity: 16 L (4.2 US gal, 3.5 Imp gal). Load limit: 5 kg (11 lb).

To close it, push down on the rear of the hood until it latches securely.

[Manual20_66]

Glove compartment:

[Manual20_67]

To open the glove compartment, slide the latch toward you and lift the lid.

[Manual20_68]

To close it, push the lid down until it locks securely.

Glove compartment capacity: 2 L (0.53 US gal, 0.44 Imp gal). Load limit: 1 kg (2.2 lb).

Fire extinguisher:

[jetski_04]

Check that a full fire extinguisher is on board. The fire extinguisher container is located in the battery compartment. Remove the seat and turn the container cap counterclockwise to open it.

[jetski_05]

After inserting the fire extinguisher, make sure the container cap is tightened securely. Always keep the extinguisher in the fire extinguisher container.

A fire extinguisher is not standard equipment. Obtain one from a dealer or fire extinguisher supplier if needed.

Required fire extinguisher classification: B-1. Capacity: 2 lb or more.

section_title: 8. Seat, Hood, Filler Caps, and Fuel Cock Operation
section_path: 8. Seat, Hood, Filler Caps, and Fuel Cock Operation
text:
# 8. Seat, Hood, Filler Caps, and Fuel Cock Operation

Seat removal and installation:

There is a seat latch at the rear of the seat.

[Manual20_35]

To remove the seat, pull the seat latch up and pull the seat off.

[Manual20_36]

To install the seat, insert the projection on the front of the seat into the stay on the deck, then push the rear of the seat down until it locks securely.

[Manual20_37]

Make sure the seat is properly secured before operating.

Hood operation:

To open the hood, push the latch down and lift the hood.

[Manual20_38]

To close the hood, push it down until it locks.

[Manual20_39]

Make sure the hood is properly secured before operating.

Fuel tank filler cap:

To remove the fuel tank filler cap, turn it counterclockwise. Make sure it is properly secured before operating.

[Manual20_40]

Oil tank filler cap:

To remove the oil tank filler cap, turn it counterclockwise. Make sure it is properly secured before operating.

[Manual20_41]

Fuel cock knob:

The fuel cock supplies fuel from the fuel tank to the carburetors.

[Manual20_42]

Fuel cock positions:

- OFF: Fuel does not flow. Always turn the fuel cock knob to OFF when the engine is not running.
- ON: Fuel flows to the carburetors. Use this position when starting and operating the watercraft.
- RES: Reserve fuel is available. Use this position if you run out of fuel while operating. Refuel as soon as possible, then turn the knob back to ON.

section_title: 9. Engine Stop, Shut-Off Cord, Starting Controls, Cooling Outlet, and Steering
section_path: 9. Engine Stop, Shut-Off Cord, Starting Controls, Cooling Outlet, and Steering
text:
# 9. Engine Stop, Shut-Off Cord, Starting Controls, Cooling Outlet, and Steering

Engine stop switch:

Push the red engine stop switch to stop the engine normally.

[Manual20_43]

Engine shut-off switch and cord:

Insert the clip on the end of the engine shut-off cord under the black engine shut-off switch. The engine stops automatically when the clip is removed, such as if the operator falls off.

[Manual20_44]

Warning: Always attach the engine shut-off cord to your wrist and the clip to the engine shut-off switch before starting the engine. To prevent accidental starting or unauthorized use, remove the clip whenever the engine is not running.

[Manual20_45]

Choke lever:

A cold engine requires a richer air-fuel mixture supplied by the choke. Move the choke lever in the indicated direction to turn the choke on, and move it back to turn the choke off.

[Manual20_46]

Throttle lever:

Squeeze the throttle lever to increase engine speed. Release it to decrease engine speed or return to idle.

[Manual20_47]

Start switch:

Push the green start switch to start the engine. The engine will not start if the clip is removed from the engine shut-off switch.

[Manual20_48]

Cooling water pilot outlet:

When the engine is running, cooling water circulates through the engine and is discharged from the pilot outlets. Check that water is being discharged from the outlets. If no water is discharged, cooling water may not be circulating. Stop the engine and check the cause. If the cooling water passages are dry, it may take about 20 seconds for water to reach the outlet after starting.

[Manual20_49]

Steering system:

Turn the handlebars in the direction you want to travel. Turning the handlebars changes the angle of the jet thrust nozzle, which changes the watercraft direction. Because jet thrust determines turning speed and direction, the throttle must usually be open when turning except at trolling speed.

[Manual20_50]

section_title: 10. QSTS Trim System and Adjustable Sponsons
section_path: 10. QSTS Trim System and Adjustable Sponsons
text:
# 10. QSTS Trim System and Adjustable Sponsons

The Quick Shift Trim System (QSTS) selector is located at the left handlebar grip and adjusts the trim angle of the watercraft by changing the vertical angle of the jet thrust nozzle.

The QSTS has five positions: two bow-down positions, neutral, and two bow-up positions.

[Manual20_51]

To change the trim angle:

1. Reduce engine speed to 3,000 r/min or less.
2. Squeeze the shift lock lever and turn the QSTS selector to the desired position.
3. Release the shift lock lever to lock the selector.

Caution: Do not turn the QSTS selector while operating at full throttle, or QSTS damage may occur.

[Manual20_52]

The neutral position provides good performance for most operating conditions.

Bow down: Turn the grip to a bow-down position and the bow will go down while the watercraft is on plane. This puts more of the bow in the water, gives the watercraft more “hook,” enhances turning performance, and helps the watercraft get on plane more quickly. At higher speeds, it may increase bow steering, wave following, fuel consumption, and reduce maximum speed.

Bow up: Turn the grip to a bow-up position and the bow will rise while on plane. This reduces water resistance, enhancing straight-ahead acceleration and top speed. In some conditions, the watercraft may porpoise, or hop. If porpoising occurs, select neutral or bow down.

[Manual20_53]

Adjustable sponsons:

The sponsons can be positioned to enhance straight-line performance or turning performance according to preference and operating conditions.

[Manual20_69]

- Up position: Less water resistance; enhances straight-ahead acceleration on plane and top speed.
- Down position: Gives the watercraft more hook; enhances turning performance.

[Manual20_70]

To adjust the sponsons:

1. Remove the bolts on both sponsons.
2. Remove both sponsons and reinstall them in the desired position.
3. Install both sponsons at the same level.
4. Tighten the bolts to 18 N·m (1.8 kgf·m, 13 ft·lb).

[Manual20_83]

[Manual20_84]

section_title: 11. Multifunction Information Center and Warning Indicators
section_path: 11. Multifunction Information Center and Warning Indicators
text:
# 11. Multifunction Information Center and Warning Indicators

The multifunction information center includes the tachometer, speedometer, fuel meter, hour meter, warning light, oil warning indicator, engine overheat warning indicator, fuel warning indicator, and reset button.

[Manual20_54]

Cautions:

- Do not run the engine at full throttle for more than 15 seconds on land to check the meter; the engine could overheat.
- Use the specified resistor-type spark plug and cap, or the meter may function erratically.

When the engine starts, all displays light up and the buzzer sounds twice. The meter operates normally after a few seconds. The current display continues for 30 seconds after the engine stops.

Tachometer:

The tachometer displays engine speed in r/min by segments. Each segment indicates 250 r/min.

[Manual20_55]

Speedometer:

The speedometer shows watercraft speed against water. If it malfunctions, “--” blinks.

[Manual20_56]

Reset button:

Pressing the reset button stops the buzzer.

[Manual20_57]

Fuel meter:

The fuel meter has eight segments to show the approximate fuel remaining. The display varies with operating condition and should be used as a reference.

[Manual20_58]
